estimated_roles.title: Talent Acquisition Specialist

estimated_roles.family: Operations (field / kitchen)
estimated_roles.why: The single largest fresher door here and the one that ties most directly to what this round funds — deepening the kitchen network in Bengaluru and Delhi-NCR. Every small kitchen needs a shift owner running throughput against a 10-minute promise, plus food cost, wastage, crew rostering and rider dispatch. Hired locally and in volume, usually without a public posting, so it will not show up on the careers page.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Inventory Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and procurement
estimated_roles.why: Swish is already hiring a Senior Manager - Inventory & Process Design and a Procurement Manager; managers hired at this stage bring one or two junior analysts under them within a quarter. Fresh food at 1M+ orders/month across ~50 pincodes makes daily demand forecasting, indent accuracy, vendor SLAs and wastage tracking a genuine analytical seat rather than a coordination one.

estimated_roles.title: City Launch Associate (New Cities)
estimated_roles.family: Operations and city launch
estimated_roles.why: The round explicitly funds entry into new Tier-1 cities, with Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad named as targets. Launch pods are small, travel-heavy and staffed at the associate layer with graduates because that is cheap and mobile: site scouting, landlord and vendor onboarding, hiring the first kitchen crews, hitting day-30 order density. Expect relocation, a six-day week and milestone-linked variable.

estimated_roles.title: Growth Marketing Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: Monthly orders tripled to 1M+ since March and the company is now buying demand in fresh pincodes it has never served. A Brand Manager and a PR Lead are already listed at the senior layer; the execution work under them — app-install campaigns, pincode-level offers, retention pushes, CRM and funnel reporting — is standard entry-level work at a consumer app and is normally the second business hire a growth-stage D2C company opens to freshers.

estimated_roles.title: Business / Operations Analyst
estimated_roles.why: Rs 4 Cr of FY25 revenue against a Rs 19 Cr loss means per-kitchen and per-order unit economics are the number the new investors will watch every month. Swish is already hiring a Manager - Operations Excellence & Productivity, and that function runs on an analyst layer. SQL, a BI tool and comfort with messy operational data are the entry ticket; an engineering graduate is well placed for this one.
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst

estimated_roles.title: Category / Menu Associate
estimated_roles.family: Category management and merchandising
estimated_roles.why: A cook-in-house model lives or dies on menu mix, price points, SKU count per kitchen and food cost per dish — the constraint is the kitchen's physical throughput, so category and ops are joined at the hip. As the kitchen count grows the menu function separates out from central ops and picks up junior support. Priced at the non-MBA graduate half of the band, not the MBA half.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / strategy
estimated_roles.why: Three founders, three rounds in 18 months, a five-city expansion to plan and a stated 1,000-kitchen ambition — the classic conditions for a one- or two-person founder's office doing investor reporting, city business cases and whatever is on fire. It is the best-paid fresher seat at this company and by far the most competitive; realistically it goes to a tier-1 campus hire or someone with a prior startup internship.

companies.fit_reason: Two forces pull opposite ways. The business genuinely absorbs graduates in volume: a dense network of company-owned kitchens, 1M+ orders a month, and a funded push into Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad produce a continuous need for kitchen-shift, hub-ops and launch associates, and those hires are made locally, quickly and in numbers. But nothing currently visible is a graduate seat. The ten non-engineering roles on LinkedIn are a Head of Human Resources, four manager/senior-manager roles, a PR Lead, a Brand Manager, an Assistant Manager - Controllership and two Maintenance Technician (PMS) trade jobs — that is a leadership-layer build-out following the raise, not campus hiring, and the technician roles are ITI/diploma seats where an engineering graduate would be both overqualified and underpaid. So the doors exist but they are mostly unposted, and most of them pay Rs 3.5-6.5L for field operations with six-day weeks and shift timings that track the lunch and dinner peaks. Only three or four seats here clear Rs 8L — supply-chain analyst, city launch, ops analyst, founder's office — and each is a one- or two-person team. One more thing to weigh: Rs 4 Cr of revenue against a Rs 19 Cr loss and a business model that requires heavy fixed physical infrastructure means the fixed cash component is the only part of an offer worth counting on, and role scope can change with the next board meeting. Good place to learn operations fast; poor place to expect a structured graduate programme or a defensible pay band.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows. Swish has published no salary band, and neither has any company in this set. Four specific weaknesses to carry forward. (1) Swish has no owned careers page or ATS — the "Careers" link on justswish.in points at LinkedIn — so the role list came from an employer-filtered LinkedIn search whose individual postings could not be opened and re-confirmed, and the two Maintenance Technician (PMS) listings in Gurugram / Greater Delhi were attributed by the listing rather than independently verified. (2) None of those listings is an entry-level business seat, so seven of the eight rows above are predictions about hiring that has not been posted, not vacancies you can apply to today. (3) The frontline kitchen, hub and rider-supervisor hiring that would actually employ most freshers here is done locally and never appears online, so its pay is inferred from Rapido, Porter and Zepto comparables rather than from Swish itself. (4) The stage is genuinely ambiguous — a "Series B extension" label on a company founded in July 2024 with Rs 4 Cr of revenue — so I priced against Series A-B and dropped confidence one step from the medium carried by the underlying rows. Engineering roles were seen on LinkedIn (Software Engineer - Infrastructure & Platform, Software Engineer - Security, Tech Lead / Engineering Manager) and deliberately excluded under the non-engineering filter; a 2026/2027 engineering graduate targeting Swish should note that the engineering track is the better-defined and better-paid entry path at this company. Check any live number against the actual offer letter and against AmbitionBox/Glassdoor entries for Swish once enough headcount accumulates to populate them.

companies.careers_url: https://in.linkedin.com/company/carrum-mobility-solutions-pvt-ltd-gurugram/jobs (no careers page exists on carrum.co.in — /careers is a hard 404 and the site's only hiring surface is driver recruitment; all corporate hiring runs through dated LinkedIn company posts with applications by email to hr@carrum.co.in)
companies.caveat: Three things could make this wrong. First, benchmark fit: every Series A-B row in the table is built from SaaS, consumer-internet and quick-commerce companies, while Carrum is an asset-heavy vehicle-leasing operator whose cost base is cars and driver payouts, not salaries. If it prices corporate ops staff against the listed-logistics market instead (Delhivery Executive Rs 2.0-4.3 LPA, Rapido Business Ops Executive Rs 2.4-4.5 LPA), real entry offers could land at Rs 3-5 LPA — below my floor. Second, Carrum may simply not hire at 0-1 yrs on the business side: every corporate posting the research surfaced specifies real experience (Program Manager 5-6 yrs, Product Manager 2-4 yrs, a Business Head, a Debt & Treasury Manager), the AI Evangelist's 0-3 window is the sole exception, and a ~150-person corporate team scaling a fleet 2x in 12 months often prefers laterals who need no training. Third, the profile records no headcount target and no hiring number anywhere in the reporting — TechCrunch says only that the company will 'hire as it scales' — so the volume and timing of every role I marked 'likely' or 'possible' is inference from what the round funds, not from anything Carrum has announced. Also note the round is small in absolute terms ($10M against a fleet-financing need for ~6,000 vehicles), which implies most of the capital goes to debt-backed asset purchase rather than payroll, and that Uber as the sole investor gives one customer unusual leverage over the cost structure.

companies.careers_url: No careers page exists. Site is marmaladedrinks.com (5 pages: /, /brightsidecraftwhiskey, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-use, /locations); every careers path 404s. Hiring runs through the homepage 'JOIN THE REVOLUTION' inbox at careers@marmaladedrinks.com, and the two live trade roles are recruited via co-founder Udit Mediratta's LinkedIn posts with applications to udit@marmaladedrinks.com. The LinkedIn company page (linkedin.com/company/marmaladedrinks) shows zero posted listings.
companies.caveat: The honest risk is that no true entry-level seat opens here at all in the next 12 months. Both roles actually being recruited ask for 2-4 years of alcobev or consumer-goods sales plus existing Mumbai trade relationships — the whole point of the hire is a contact book a 2026/2027 graduate does not have. A company of 5-15 people with Rs 6 crore in the bank buys perhaps 3-6 more heads total, and at a tripling-revenue target it buys experienced closers before it buys trainees. Second, alcobev field sales recruits from FMCG, hospitality and liquor-distribution backgrounds, not engineering campuses; an engineering degree is neutral-to-negative signal for these specific seats unless paired with genuine on-ground sales interest. Third, everything below the two named roles is inference from what the round funds, not from any posting — there is no ATS, no recruiter and no job board footprint, so a role could appear and be filled through the founder's network without ever being visible. Fourth, the pay band rests on a benchmark row the source itself marks medium-confidence with no stage-tagged Indian alcobev data behind it, and a company this small can price a first junior hire almost anywhere within or below it. Finally, on the upside: because hiring is founder-inbox based, a direct, well-argued email to Udit Mediratta proposing a junior territory or activation role is a more realistic path in than waiting for a posting to appear.

companies.caveat: The single biggest risk is that none of the forecast roles ever gets posted. QNu's live board has 18 reqs and not one entry-level seat of any kind — the four non-engineering roles are 3-10 years, and a 2016-vintage, ~140-person hardware company that has hired exclusively experienced people for a decade may simply have no graduate business rung. Deep-tech GTM into defence, PSU banks and government also tends to be hired through founder networks and ex-defence/telco/PSU operators, not campus-style intake, so the commercial build-out implied by the round could happen entirely off-market. Second, the benchmark rows are built almost wholly from consumer internet and SaaS companies; a quantum-security hardware firm with multi-year government procurement cycles typically pays its business side more conservatively, so the band could sit 1-2 LPA high in practice — the floor is likelier than the ceiling. Third, the stage label is genuinely ambiguous: "Series A1" with Rs 375 Cr raised over ten years behaves like Series B/C on capital while the business org is seed-thin; if you price it off the Series C+ metro BD row instead, the band moves up to roughly Rs 6.5-12L fixed. Fourth, and most likely to matter for an engineering graduate specifically: if QNu hires you into a customer-facing ENGINEERING title (Application Engineer, Field/Deployment Engineer, Solutions Engineer) rather than a business title, you are paid off the engineering band, which at a funded Bengaluru deep-tech hardware company runs materially higher than anything in this table. The title on the offer letter, not the actual work, decides the number — so push for the engineering-coded title if the work is the same. Finally, the board was last updated 2026-07-27 and the round closed 2026-09-09, so everything post-raise is unobserved; re-check the greytHR feed directly (qnulabs.com/careers only redirects, the zohorecruit board is dead, and Uplers' listing is wrong on both funding and role count).

companies.caveat: Four things could make this wrong. (2) Theater posts no salary anywhere and has no careers page, so there is no company-specific data point to anchor on; every number here is inferred from comparable D2C and category roles elsewhere. (3) Role mix risk cuts both ways: the Tracxn jump from 56 to 421 headcount is almost certainly store and warehouse staff, and if an engineering graduate is hired into a store-operations or retail-launch seat rather than a corporate analyst seat, the real offer is Rs 3-4L, below this band's midpoint; conversely, if Theater decides it needs a genuine marketplace-analytics or founder's-office hire post-raise, a single competitive offer could clear Rs 7-8L and sit above the band. (4) The company is currently hiring zero engineering or product roles - all nine to ten live openings are commerce, supply chain, finance, CX and creative - so an engineering graduate is competing on business skills, not a technical degree, and would be benchmarked against commerce and MBA candidates, not against software pay. Also note the stage itself is slightly ambiguous: Rs 56.25 crore in filings versus Rs 75 crore announced, and at Rs 33 crore revenue the round is large relative to the business, so hiring could accelerate faster than a typical Series A pace.

companies.caveat: The biggest risk is that this company opens no entry-level graduate seat at all in the next few quarters. There is no careers page, no hiring number anywhere in the funding coverage, two of the three third-party boards are empty, and the single live posting is one Relationship Manager in Pune — a ~50-person company recruiting reactively through LinkedIn and recruiter networks. Everything above except that one role is inference from what the round funds, not from an observed requisition. Second, the roles they do open are a poor fit for the stated candidate: pharma-distribution Relationship Manager postings almost always ask for one to three years of field sales experience in pharma, FMCG or B2B distribution and value an existing distributor rolodex over a fresh engineering degree, so a 2026/2027 B.E./B.Tech grad is competing against a candidate profile the company prefers — and where they do hire freshers into these seats, the CTC is often 60-70% fixed with the balance riding on collections, which makes headline numbers misleading. Third, the stage label is doing real work in the band: if you treat this as a genuine Series A the floor is 5+, and if you treat $4M on a $3M seed as a seed extension the floor is 3.5, and I cannot tell you with confidence which one their offer letters reflect. Fourth, the location split matters — a Mumbai HQ analyst seat and a Pune or tier-2 field seat at the same company can differ by 30-40% on the same title. Finally, the round was announced two days ago; postings may well follow within a month and would supersede all of this. Treat these as benchmark-derived estimates, not Fundly.ai's stated bands.

estimated_roles.title: Merchandising / Category Associate

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the split is sharp: Mokobara hires plenty of freshers, but mostly into the wrong roles for an engineering graduate. The company runs 50+ stores and is opening more, so store and retail-ops hiring is near-continuous — those jobs are genuinely open to a 0-1 year candidate and pay Rs 3-5.5L, which is below what most 2026/2027 engineering graduates will accept and is not an analytical career track. The HQ roles worth having (growth, planning, merchandising, finance) sit in a corporate team that is likely well under 100 people, so there are only a handful of seats and they are usually filled at 1-3 years of experience rather than off-campus. The hard evidence supports that reading: careers.mokobara.com is a creative-team-only microsite that currently ships an empty positions array and says every seat is taken, mokobara.com has no careers link at all, and the entire verifiable live hiring worldwide on 2026-09-10 is one LinkedIn posting — Finance Specialist — which is non-engineering and already had 200+ applicants a day after going up. Against that: revenue nearly doubled to Rs 230.2 Cr, the round funds store expansion and a UAE build-out, and a D2C brand at that growth rate genuinely needs junior performance-marketing and planning analysts. The realistic path is not the careers page. It is careers@mokobara.com plus Naukri and Instahyre, targeting performance marketing or demand planning, and treating store management as a fallback rather than the goal.
companies.careers_url: https://careers.mokobara.com/ (creative-team-only microsite, Bengaluru, explicitly no remote — it currently advertises zero roles of any kind; the live Finance Specialist posting is on Mokobara's LinkedIn company feed, and the general route in is careers@mokobara.com, with store and retail-ops roles appearing on Naukri and Instahyre)
companies.caveat: These are estimates derived from benchmarks.json, not published salary ranges — Mokobara has never disclosed a band, and neither the Finance Specialist posting nor any other listing states pay. Confidence is set low deliberately: the underlying Series C+ rows are medium-confidence at best and are built from tech-platform comparables, so every band here required a judgement-based downward sector adjustment to a physical consumer-goods brand that no source measures directly. Five of the six roles are predictions, not observations — only Finance Specialist is a verified live posting, and it is non-engineering and probably wants 1-3 years. Two further Mokobara roles surfaced in research (a Retail Store Manager on Instahyre and a National Account Manager - Retail on getmereferred) but could not be loaded to confirm they are live, so 'one open role' reflects what is publicly verifiable today, not the company's true hiring volume, which is almost certainly higher on the store side. Headcount (201-500 on LinkedIn, versus 11-50 in some directories that appear to count only head office) and the legal entity name are estimates, not filings-verified. Round identity is confirmed against the tracker entry on all five fields: Series C, Rs 170 Cr, Sauce.vc plus four co-investors, founded 2019, 2026-09-05.

For a D2C beauty brand in that position, CAC and ROAS on Meta/Google/marketplace ads are the one lever that moves both revenue and burn, and paid-media execution is the last thing a D2C brand stops staffing. It is also the cheapest seat to fill with a 0-1 year hire.

Investor reporting packs and unit-economics dashboards are entry-level analyst work, and a stabilisation raise funds cost visibility before it funds growth.

estimated_roles.title: Category / Merchandising Executive (colour cosmetics)
estimated_roles.family: Category management and merchandising
estimated_roles.why: Colour cosmetics is an assortment and shade-depth business, and a stabilisation phase means SKU rationalisation, dead-inventory clean-up and margin-mix work rather than new-category launches. That is exactly what a junior category executive does, and it directly frees working capital, which is what the round is for.

estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: When own-site acquisition is unaffordable, marketplace channels carry the volume. Listing hygiene, catalogue and A+ content, marketplace ad spend and co-op negotiation is a junior account-executive seat, and it is revenue-protecting rather than revenue-expanding, which fits a survival raise.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Demand Planning Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Inventory is the largest cash lever available to a brand raising to stabilise. Better forecasting, fill-rate and returns control at the warehouse and counter level converts directly into cash, and planning-executive seats are the standard entry point for that work.

estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch

estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: The standard playbook when paid acquisition has to shrink is to push repeat purchase through email, WhatsApp and loyalty. A junior CRM associate is a cheap way to lift contribution margin without adding ad spend, which is precisely what a stabilisation raise pays for.

estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Down-round companies commonly add one junior associate to the CEO/CFO office to run the cost programme, board and investor reporting and A91's diligence follow-ups. It is a single seat at most, and it is the first thing cut if hiring stays frozen.

companies.careers_url: None found. sugarcosmetics.com has no careers page (its pages sitemap lists only /pages/about-us; /pages/careers and /careers redirect to product pages and /pages/career returns 404), careers.sugarcosmetics.com does not resolve, and no ATS instance exists on keka, darwinbox, zohorecruit or freshteam. companies.caveat: The most likely way this is wrong is that SUGAR opens none of these roles at all. There is no use-of-funds statement, no headcount plan, no careers page, no ATS and no public postings, and the round reads as a survival raise on falling revenue and doubling losses — a company in that position often freezes corporate hiring entirely and backfills only retail and field seats, where an engineering graduate is not the target candidate anyway. Two further specific risks. One, if they do hire on the business side, a cash-constrained company usually buys experienced laterals who need no training rather than 0-1 year graduates, which would push the real entry door to internships and contract roles rather than the full-time bands quoted here. Two, the evidence base for the "no hiring" read is weak in a particular way: the research session's web-search budget was exhausted and mine is too, so job boards (Naukri, Indeed, foundit, Instahyre, AmbitionBox) were never actually checked — all returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches. Absence of a findable posting is not a confirmed empty board, and a brand this size almost certainly recruits through Naukri and referrals rather than an owned careers page, so live openings could well exist that this analysis cannot see. The company profile itself is marked unverified, including the headcount range and the stage read. Finally, the benchmark rows used carry medium confidence at best, none of them segment by funding stage directly, and none cover a distressed down-round company specifically — the stabilisation discount applied here is judgement, not measurement.

estimated_roles.title: D2C / Performance Marketing Associate (international launch)
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: The round is explicitly partly for launching distribution in markets beyond Poland, and the company already sells five SKUs direct-to-consumer on its own Shopify store with, by its own account, effectively no marketing spend to date. That is the single clearest commercial gap the money creates: someone to run paid social/search, marketplace listings and lifecycle email for the Miorelaxant Magic line. Marked 'possible' rather than 'likely' because the careers page shows zero commercial hiring today - all three postings are EU-grant lab/production staffing - and because any such hire would almost certainly sit in Warsaw or in a target EU market, not in India. An Indian graduate realistically reaches this only as a remote contractor doing performance-marketing execution for an EU brand.

estimated_roles.title: International Distribution / E-commerce Business Development Associate
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: Their B2B channel is aesthetic-medicine clinics and their B2C channel is a single-country Shopify store; taking either into new markets needs someone doing distributor outreach, marketplace and reseller onboarding, order and pricing admin. Ties directly to the stated use of funds (international distribution). Again 'possible' only - a four-founder Polish lab company expanding into EU markets hires this in-market or through a distributor, and there is no India entity, no India-facing product and no evidence of any remote commercial hiring. Language is a hard filter too: the careers page and postings are Polish-only.

companies.fit_reason: This is not an Indian company and has no India presence, so for a 2026/2027 Indian engineering graduate the realistic answer is that there is nothing here. Three compounding reasons. First, scale: under 15 people including part-timers, a core of four founding scientists plus an advisor, and a round of EUR 1.6m against a Polish cost base - that headcount does not support a business-track graduate programme of any kind. Second, what is actually open: the two roles named in the profile - "Specjalista/Specjalistka ds. formulacji bazy produktow" and "Specjalista ds. oczyszczania bialek rekombinowanych" - are laboratory science roles (cosmetic base formulation, recombinant protein purification), not business track, and they are grant-staffing for one specific EU project (FENG.01.01-IP.01-A09Z/24) rather than post-round commercial hiring; one is an umowa zlecenie contract and the third posting on the page requires 10+ years. I have therefore not listed them as roles, since they fall outside the business-track brief and are inaccessible to a fresh engineering graduate. Third, access: the careers page is Polish-language only (the /en/ locale serves the same Polish text), the work is Warsaw on-site lab and production, and Poland's work-permit route for a fresh non-EU graduate into a sub-15-person company is heavy. Notably, despite the round being partly for international expansion, there is no commercial, marketing or sales posting on the page at all - so even the two roles I priced above are inferred needs, not observed openings. The only plausible path for an Indian graduate is a remote freelance/contract performance-marketing or e-commerce engagement, which is a gig, not a campus-track job.
companies.caveat: These are estimates derived from India entry-level benchmark rows; Science4Beauty has published no salary band, and neither role priced above is currently advertised. Two specific warnings. (1) The company is Polish, not Indian: the export's "17.5Cr" is a currency-normalised rendering of the EUR 1.6m / ~USD 1.9m seed, not evidence of an Indian entity - do not treat this as a domestic lead. Applying Indian LPA bands to it is a hypothetical exercise about a remote India-based hire, not a read of a real India job market. (2) Both benchmark rows I used are self-described as the weakest cells in the table (no source isolates seed-stage, non-metro entry pay), the headcount is a LinkedIn band rather than a verified figure, and the company is tiny - so I lowered confidence a step and it sits at low. Use the exact domain science4beauty.net for any enrichment; .com and .pl do not resolve.

estimated_roles.title: Single Window Operator
estimated_roles.family: Branch banking (teller / customer service)
estimated_roles.why: Listed now. The classic SFB branch teller-plus-service seat, and the single most fresher-accessible title on the board by volume — 160+ branches with more coming means a steady intake. It is also the clearest illustration of why fit is only mixed: this is a Rs 2-3.5 LPA bank cadre role and an engineering graduate would be badly under-using the degree. Commerce graduates are the usual hire.

estimated_roles.title: Officer Trainee / Probationary Officer - Branch Banking (batch intake)
estimated_roles.family: Management trainee / graduate programme
estimated_roles.why: Predicted, not currently listed. Small finance banks scaling a branch network typically run periodic PO or officer-trainee batches that are recruited off-board through campus tie-ups and banking-institute channels rather than the Kula job board. Branch and deposit expansion funded by this round is exactly the trigger. This is the most structured graduate door Slice is likely to open, and it still pays on a bank cadre scale, not a startup one.

companies.fit_reason: Two different employers share one careers page, and only one of them hires graduates into business roles. The Bengaluru corporate side is almost entirely experienced-hire: AVP - AML, Branch Head, Payroll Manager, Management Auditor, Internal Auditor, Technical Program Manager II, Manager - Information System Audit, Senior Product Analyst. A 2026/27 engineering graduate has essentially one clean door there — Product Manager Intern — plus a realistic shot at Fraud Analyst or an analytics associate seat if the team opens a junior rung. The branch side, by contrast, hires freshers in volume: Single Window Operator, KYC Associate, Customer Experience Executive and Relationship Officer are all any-graduate cadres, and 160+ branches expanding on new deposit capital will keep hiring them. But those roles pay Rs 2.2-4.5 LPA, sit in Guwahati and across Assam/Odisha, and give an engineering degree no premium whatsoever — the graduate would be competing with and paid like a commerce graduate. So the honest read is not "good" and not "poor": there is real fresher hiring here, it is just concentrated in the half of the company that does not want an engineering graduate, while the half that would value one hires at Manager grade and above. An engineering graduate wanting Slice specifically should target the tech track instead — 15 of the 40 listed roles are engineering — and expect roughly two to three times the business-track number.
companies.caveat: Every number here is an estimate derived from benchmark rows plus judgement adjustments. Slice has published no salary band, and none of these figures came from the company, a job posting or an offer letter. Confidence is marked low for three specific reasons rather than as a general hedge. First, the stage genuinely straddles two benchmark rows: the export calls it Series D, but the raising entity is Slice Small Finance Bank Ltd (CIN U65100AS2016PLC017505), a profitable ~3,400-person licensed bank, so startup rows over-read and listed/large rows under-read it. Second, no benchmark family in the file covers Indian branch banking cadres — Single Window Operator, Relationship Officer and KYC Associate had to be priced by overriding the ops and BD rows downward rather than by reading a row, and those are precisely the roles a fresher is most likely to actually get. Third, the field and branch bands are CTC including incentive, and at Indian banks the fixed portion is commonly only 60-75% of that, so a Rs 4 LPA offer may be Rs 2.8 LPA guaranteed. Also note: the careers board is a live snapshot as of 2026-09-10 and will drift, several listed field roles show location as "India" or a state with workplace "remote" in the board data but are almost certainly branch-network field jobs rather than work-from-home, and other listed field-sales titles not priced individually here (Relationship Officer - Merchant, Branch Sales Manager) sit in or above the same band as Relationship Officer- Liability. Finally, the identity match was confirmed by triangulating investor, amount and date — "Slice" collides with a US pizza-software company, an insurer and two other firms, so any independent verification should check it is Slice Small Finance Bank being described.

estimated_roles.title: Growth / Performance Marketing Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: Ultrahuman is a direct-to-consumer hardware and subscription business selling in 180+ countries — paid acquisition, creator/affiliate and lifecycle marketing are the core commercial engine, and the round explicitly funds market expansion into India and the UAE. This is the single most reliable business-track entry door at a D2C brand of this size.

estimated_roles.title: Business / Data Analyst (D2C growth and retention analytics)
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: 800,000 rings sold plus CGM, Home and Blood Vision subscriptions generates heavy demand for cohort, churn, attach-rate and unit-economics reporting. An engineering grad with SQL and Python is a natural fit, and this is the role a 0-1 year technical fresher is most likely to actually land on the business side here.

estimated_roles.title: Customer Experience / Member Support Associate
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (customer operations sub-ladder)
estimated_roles.why: A global consumer medical-adjacent device with subscriptions, RMAs, shipping across 180+ countries, and a disclosed June 2026 wellness-data breach carries a large and permanent support load. High-volume, genuinely fresher-friendly, and pays accordingly.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Operations Associate (device inventory, RMA, fulfilment)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Physical hardware built partly in Texas and sold worldwide, plus consumable CGM sensors and blood-test logistics, needs demand planning, 3PL coordination and reverse-logistics execution. Offline retail expansion multiplies this work.

estimated_roles.title: Retail Store Associate / Experience Associate (Ultrahuman experience store)
estimated_roles.family: Retail and field operations (priced off the Operations hub/store ladder)
estimated_roles.why: The round's stated first use is offline expansion via physical stores and offline touchpoints in India and the UAE. Every store opened creates several of these seats — the highest-volume fresher hiring this raise will produce. Almost certainly does not require an engineering degree.

estimated_roles.title: Retail Expansion / City Launch Associate (India and UAE offline)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (central/city-launch ladder)
estimated_roles.why: The central counterpart to the store seat: site scouting, mall and distributor negotiation support, launch checklists, store P&L tracking as they enter new Indian cities and the UAE. Directly funded by this round.

estimated_roles.title: Associate Product Manager / Product Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM)
estimated_roles.why: The round's platform thesis — turning the ring from a tracker into an ambient computing platform running third-party PowerPlugs apps, the reason Qualcomm Ventures invested — needs product bodies. But a ~500-person hardware company rarely runs a structured APM programme; expect one or two opportunistic hires, usually favouring 1-3 years of experience or a tier-1 MBA over a 0-1 year grad.

estimated_roles.title: Associate, Founder's Office / Business Strategy
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Founder-led company (Mohit Kumar, Vatsal Singhal) in a multi-geography expansion year with live patent litigation against Oura and a new debt facility to manage — classic conditions for a generalist analyst seat reporting to the founders. Typically one or two seats total, filled through referral.

estimated_roles.title: Business Development Associate, UltraWork (enterprise / corporate wellness)
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: UltraWork is the employer-facing offering and is the obvious secondary revenue line to push post-raise. Entry BD/inside-sales seats are the standard fresher door into B2B, though at Ultrahuman this motion is small next to D2C so headcount will be thin.

companies.fit_reason: Two things pull in opposite directions. In favour: this is a genuinely well-funded consumer brand in the fresher's own city, and the money it just raised goes into offline retail in India and the UAE — store, customer-experience and fulfilment seats that hire 0-1 year candidates in volume and hire them soon. Against: as of today the careers portal (Zoho Recruit) renders "Currently we don't have any open jobs at Ultrahuman" and the underlying public API returns an empty job list, so there is nothing at all to apply to right now — zero roles, not merely zero non-engineering ones. Beyond that, Ultrahuman is a hardware-and-clinical-science company: its centre of gravity is embedded/firmware, app engineering, industrial design and clinical research, so the business-side org is thin relative to a marketplace or SaaS firm of the same revenue, and the two seats an engineering graduate would actually want — APM and growth analyst — are few, competitive, and usually go to someone with 1-3 years or a tier-1 MBA. The realistic fresher entry points here (retail store, member support, fulfilment ops) pay Rs 3.5-6.5L, materially below what a 2026/27 B.E./B.Tech graduate typically targets, and they are not a stepping stone into product without a deliberate internal move. The clinical-research hiring this round funds is largely closed to an engineering degree — those seats want life-sciences or biomedical backgrounds. Worth tracking closely rather than counting on: a company that just took $70M and has an empty job board is about to reopen it.
companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. Ultrahuman has published no salary band for any role, and no offer data specific to this company was available — every figure is an inference from India-wide entry-level comparables adjusted for stage, city and role, not something the company has stated. Four specific health warnings. First, none of these titles is confirmed: the careers page is live and genuinely empty today, so unlike a company with an open board, there are no "listed now" roles here and every title above is my prediction of what they will open, not a posting you can check. Titles may differ in wording (for example "Retail Experience Specialist" rather than "Retail Store Associate"). Second, the round label in the export understates the event — Rs 47.2 Cr "Venture Debt" from Alteria Capital is the ~$5M debt slice of a $70M equity-and-debt raise announced 3 Sep 2026; anyone sizing hiring off the Rs 47.2 Cr figure alone would badly underestimate this company. Third, the name collides: an unrelated "ULTRA HUMAN" sporting-goods manufacturer (2-10 employees) shares the LinkedIn name, and theorg.com lists "Ultrahuman" at 11-50 employees; both would produce a wildly wrong read of scale. The company priced here is the Bengaluru smart-ring firm founded by Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal. Fourth, the benchmark rows themselves are built mostly from SaaS, fintech and quick-commerce salary data, with no Indian consumer-hardware brand in the sample — I have adjusted for that, but the adjustment is judgement, not measurement, which is why confidence stays at medium even though the underlying company profile is verified. Retail store, customer-support and fulfilment bands in particular are set far below the SaaS-built comparables in the benchmark file, deliberately.

estimated_roles.title: Operations Associate

estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Listed for Bengaluru on 2026-09-03. Central command-centre seat monitoring battery telemetry, station faults and swap SLAs across cities - a shift-rostered monitoring role, the standard fresher entry point in an asset-heavy network business, and one that scales linearly as the fleet doubles.

estimated_roles.title: Network Expansion Executive (swap-station site acquisition)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: The stated use of funds is expanding swapping infrastructure and doubling the fleet over 12-18 months. That work is site scouting, landlord/host negotiation, permissions and station commissioning in new micro-markets - a junior field seat that always sits under the City Manager roles Yuma is already hiring (Hyderabad).

estimated_roles.title: Fleet Sales Executive / B2B Account Executive (fleet and OEM accounts)
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: The round explicitly funds broadening the customer base beyond Yulu to third-party fleet operators, OEMs and retail EV owners. Signing delivery fleets and small 3W operators city by city is feet-on-street B2B sales, and a Regional Business Head is already open in Delhi NCR - senior GTM hires of that kind are normally followed by junior reps under them.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain and Procurement Executive (battery packs and charging hardware)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Yuma builds its own packs and charging hardware in Chennai and Bengaluru and has just acquired battery-tech firm Grinntech. Doubling the fleet means doubling cell, BMS and enclosure inflow - a planning/vendor-follow-up seat that manufacturers routinely fill with fresh engineering graduates.

estimated_roles.title: Operations / Fleet Data Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: 50,000 swaps a day, 60M cumulative swaps and an EBITDA break-even target inside two quarters make station-density, battery-utilisation and cost-per-swap analysis a real function. A Business Finance Manager is already open in Bengaluru, which usually implies analyst support underneath.

estimated_roles.title: Management Trainee - Business Operations
estimated_roles.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programmes
estimated_roles.why: Magna, a ~$40B listed Tier-1 auto supplier, runs graduate trainee programmes as standard practice, and a JV scaling from 18 cities needs a bench of city-ops leads. A rotational MT track through station ops, supply chain and city launch is the cheapest way to build it.

estimated_roles.title: Finance / MIS Analyst (business finance)
estimated_roles.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programmes
estimated_roles.why: An open Business Finance Manager role plus a public commitment to EBITDA profitability by FY27 implies city-level P&L reporting, subscription revenue reconciliation and capex tracking on a doubling asset base - work that gets pushed to a junior analyst.

companies.fit_reason: Yuma does hire freshers, but almost entirely into one lane: shift-rostered field and control-room operations at roughly ₹3-5 LPA. The Operations Associate posting is explicitly entry-level with rotating shifts, and the company also ran blue-collar Commander/Helper postings on apna.co in July 2026 - that is the shape of its junior intake. The business-track ladder above it is closed to graduates: all three of the other live roles (City Manager - Operations, Business Finance Manager, Regional Business Head) need 4-10 years. There is no APM, no growth-marketing seat, no graduate analyst programme visible, and no engineering role at all on the feed, which tells you the ₹335 Cr is funding stations, batteries and field headcount rather than an HQ hiring wave. So: a genuine, real entry point for a graduate who wants asset-heavy operations experience in EV infrastructure with a large listed parent behind it and a plausible path to city-ops leadership - and a poor fit for anyone targeting a product, strategy, analytics or brand-name-pay first job. Also note the shifts and the field posting locations are not negotiable in these roles.
companies.caveat: Estimates from benchmarks - Yuma has published no salary band, and no source states one. Specific cautions: (1) The company's own careers page renders "0+ Job openings" and pushes everything to https://www.linkedin.com/company/magna-yuma-energy/jobs/ - the two "listed now" titles come from that LinkedIn feed as of 2026-09-10, and the Operations Associate posting was spot-verified as entry-level, but LinkedIn feeds go stale fast; check both before applying. (2) Three of the five live roles - City Manager - Operations (Hyderabad), Business Finance Manager (Bengaluru), Regional Business Head (Delhi NCR) - are deliberately excluded above because they are mid-to-senior seats, not fresher roles, despite being open today. (3) The six predicted roles are inferences from the stated use of funds (doubling the battery fleet, expanding stations, selling beyond Yulu, in-house battery tech via the Grinntech acquisition); none is confirmed to be opening. (4) Confidence lowered one step to low because the stage is genuinely ambiguous - the export says Series A and founded 2023, but the economics and the parent are Series B/C-plus - and because every benchmark row I used is built from quick-commerce, logistics and SaaS comparables rather than from EV battery-swapping, where no stage-tagged India data exists. (5) The export's "parent: Yulu" is stale; Magna is the controlling parent and sets the pay scale. (6) Do not confuse this company with Yuma Energy Inc., the unrelated Houston oil-and-gas firm - any US result under that name is the wrong employer.

Sells fleets to corporates, logistics and delivery operators — a channel BGauss needs because B2B volume fills the Chakan line faster than one-scooter-at-a-time retail. estimated_roles.title: MIS Executive
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: Listed in Hyderabad, 1-5 years, described as back office and data entry. A dealer network going from 120 to 500 outlets generates sales, stock and claims reporting that someone has to consolidate, so more of these will open as the network grows. Priced far below the analyst row's Rs 4-11L range because MIS Executive in India is an Excel-and-reporting seat, not a BI role — the row's own note warns a non-metro posting at this stage is usually the lower-priced city-analytics variant.

estimated_roles.title: Service Technician – Task Force
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (field service)
estimated_roles.why: Listed in Pune with all-India travel, and included because it is genuinely open, not because it fits. Priced at the lower half of the ops row (Rs 2.6-9L), which already contains comparable physical-ops data. Listed here so the graduate can rule it out knowingly rather than apply into it.

estimated_roles.title: Territory Sales Executive (EV Two-Wheelers)
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: The single most predictable hire from this round. Going from ~120 to 500 dealerships needs feet on the street covering assigned districts, pushing retail volume through dealer counters and chasing the monthly registration number that BGauss is publicising. OEMs hire freshers into exactly this. Priced off the BD Series C+ other-city row (Rs 5-10L) with a ~40% haircut to Indian two-wheeler territory-sales reality; expect a large monthly incentive on top of the fixed figure.

estimated_roles.title: Dealer Development Executive
estimated_roles.family: Business development and channel expansion
estimated_roles.why: Ties to the round more directly than any other role: the money is explicitly for distribution, and the stated target is roughly quadrupling the outlet count. This is the person who scouts partners, evaluates showroom locations, runs onboarding and gets a new outlet trading. Slightly above plain territory sales because it involves partner negotiation and travel. Same BD other-city row, haircut applied but held at the upper end of the field-sales spread.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Production Planning Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: The round funds capacity expansion beyond the current ~100,000 units a year at Chakan. Scaling a line means materials planning, vendor scheduling, inbound logistics and inventory control — and this is the one family where a fresh mechanical or production engineering degree is the actual qualification rather than a tolerated substitute. Priced from the ops row's middle (Rs 2.6-9L) without a haircut, since that row's Pune and manufacturing data points already match this employer type.

estimated_roles.title: Management Trainee / Graduate Trainee – Sales & Marketing
estimated_roles.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programmes
estimated_roles.why: RR Global is an established group with the scale to run a rotational intake, and a subsidiary tripling its retail volume is the natural place to put trainees. Marked possible rather than likely because no BGauss graduate programme is visible and there is no careers page to host one. Priced off the MT Series C+ other-city row (Rs 6-11L) with a heavy cut — that row describes late-stage startup trainees, and its own note says non-metro MT points run Rs 4.5-6L, which is where a manufacturer's programme actually sits.

estimated_roles.title: Marketing Executive – Retail & Brand Activation
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: A scooter priced from Rs 94,990 is sold at the showroom and at local events, not through a CAC dashboard, so the marketing hire here is retail activation, dealer co-op campaigns and test-ride drives rather than performance media. That is why the band sits well under the growth-marketing Series C+ other-city row (Rs 6-13L), which prices digital growth roles at VC-backed consumer companies — roughly a 45% cut to OEM field-marketing pay. Possible rather than likely: a 630-person OEM may keep this in a small central team in Pune.

companies.fit_reason: The volume argument is real: headcount went from roughly 338 in May 2025 to about 633 by July 2026, retail registrations tripled year-on-year, and the stated plan is to take the dealer network from ~120 outlets to 500. You cannot quadruple a dealer network without hiring a lot of junior territory sales, dealer-development and after-sales people, and OEMs fill those seats with fresh graduates because the work is legwork, not judgment. So openings will exist. What makes this mixed rather than good is the shape of them. All three roles visible today ask for experience — 2-6 years, 1-5 years, 1-3 years — and none is a fresher req. There is no campus programme, no careers page and no graduate track to apply to; hiring runs through LinkedIn and Indian job boards, which favours the lateral hire with two years at Bajaj or Ather over a 2026 B.E. graduate. And the business-track entry point here is a field or plant job in a tier-2 posting at Rs 3-6L, not an HQ analyst desk — a graduate benchmarking against a Series C+ software offer will find this well below it. The honest read: strong odds of getting hired, modest pay, and the roles are closer to the mechanical/production and channel side of an auto company than to the analytics-and-strategy work "business track" usually implies. Best route in is the Chakan plant supply-chain and planning side, where a mechanical or production engineering degree is actually the qualification rather than a nice-to-have.
companies.caveat: Three things could make this wrong. First, there is no first-party careers page — bgauss.com/careers and /career both 404, and Naukri, Indeed, Glassdoor, Foundit and Shine all blocked the scrape — so the "listed now" set is three third-party listings and is a floor, not a picture; BGauss may already be running fresher intake I cannot see. Second, the stage label is doing damage: the benchmark's "Series C+" rows describe VC-backed startups, while BGauss is a conglomerate subsidiary taking a promoter-funded round, and the size of my OEM haircut is judgment, not an observed BGauss offer — no BGauss salary data was reachable. Third, the error runs both ways. If RR Global extends a group campus MT programme to BGauss's Pune HQ, corporate trainee offers could sit at Rs 6-9L, above everything I have listed. If instead the 120-to-500 dealer push is staffed the way two-wheeler OEMs usually staff it, real offers land at Rs 2.5-3.5L fixed with most upside in monthly retail incentive, below my low ends. Every band assumes the graduate is willing to take a field or plant role in a tier-2 posting.

estimated_roles.title: Business Development Executive (supplier and buyer acquisition)
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: A B2B trade marketplace has one growth engine: getting more vetted suppliers onto the catalogue and converting inbound RFQs into transactions. With ₹6.30 crore of self-reported GMV and a live /rfq flow in the product, the seat that moves the number is someone calling agri and industrial SMEs across the Panipat-Sonipat-NCR belt to list them, then chasing buyers on the other side. This is the hire a company this size makes first and the one most open to a 0-1 year graduate. Expect fixed-plus-incentive (70:30 is the Indian norm), so the top of the band is only reached at full attainment.

estimated_roles.title: Export / Trade Operations Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: The round is explicitly described as funding deeper international trade partnerships, and the company claims operations touching Kenya, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Turkey, Iraq and Canada. Cross-border trade needs someone doing RFQ coordination, quotation follow-up, supplier vetting and export documentation (INCOTERMS, LC, DGFT paperwork). Banded slightly above the pure BD seat because documentation literacy carries a small premium and is harder to backfill — but the eight-country claim is self-reported and unaudited, so in practice this may be one person doing email follow-up rather than real trade ops.

estimated_roles.title: Digital Marketing Executive — KARM Solutions
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: KARM Solutions is a delivery agency selling SEO, web development and performance marketing to SMEs, and agencies staff delivery with freshers by design — it is the standard entry point into this business. It is also the cheapest seat in the company: agency delivery benchmarks to the low mode of the marketing band (executing client campaigns on someone else's budget), not to an in-house growth role owning P&L.

estimated_roles.title: Supplier Onboarding / Category Associate
estimated_roles.family: Category management and merchandising
estimated_roles.why: The marketplace's stated value proposition is vetted suppliers across agri-commodities, food, industrial goods and raw materials — somebody has to build and clean that catalogue, verify GST and export credentials, and structure the product taxonomy. Banded below the metro category row because at this headcount the job is catalogue operations and vendor verification, not category P&L; the Category Manager title and its pay do not exist at a 15-person company.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office / Business Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Post-raise, founders at this stage often add one generalist for investor reporting, the media/podcast arm and partnership coordination. Highest band of the five because the seat is scoped by the founder and can be negotiated individually — but the caveat matters more than the band: the published metro founder's-office range runs to ₹11L fixed and that top cluster is YC/Peak XV-backed companies hiring tier-1 campus grads. With three of six named leaders from one family, this is the bottom cluster — an ops-and-EA hybrid, not a strategy seat.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the two halves point in opposite directions. In favour: this is genuinely a company that hires 0-1 year graduates — a 15-person B2B marketplace staffs supplier calling, RFQ follow-up, catalogue building and agency delivery with freshers because that is what it can afford, and there is a real live product (the marketplace app is up and functioning) rather than a pitch deck. A graduate joining now would touch trade operations, sales and category work directly and report to a founder, which is real early exposure. Against: there is no careers page, no campus process and no listing anywhere, so hiring runs entirely through the founder's network and a cold applicant has no route in except a direct LinkedIn approach to Manav Dahuja or Kashish Goyal. Pay sits at the bottom of the seed band, ₹3.5-6L fixed, with a heavy incentive component in the sales seats. And the runway maths is unforgiving: ₹1 crore against a 15-25 person payroll is roughly 6-12 months of cover unless the GMV genuinely converts to revenue, so an offer carries employment risk a Series A company's would not. For an engineering graduate specifically, none of these roles use the degree — they are calling, Excel and documentation seats. Worth taking as a first job if it is the offer in hand and you have met the founder; not worth choosing over a structured programme at a larger employer.
companies.careers_url: None exists. Verified across all three surfaces: https://www.karmbaba.com/ is a React SPA whose JS bundle declares only /, /login, /register, /dashboard, /products, /suppliers and /rfq routes — no careers route, and /careers, /jobs and /join-us return the same 1,453-byte shell as a nonsense URL; https://www.karmsolutions.com/ nav is only about/services/portfolio/podcast/contact; https://in.linkedin.com/company/karmbaba has an empty jobs tab. Nothing on Naukri, Indeed, Internshala or LinkedIn Jobs. The realistic application route is a direct approach to the founder on LinkedIn.
companies.caveat: The honest reason this could be wrong is that it may describe hiring that never happens. Every role here is predicted, not observed — there is no careers page to check against, and a ₹1 crore raise may fund nothing beyond the founders' own runway and a contractor or two. Beyond that: (1) the stage label overstates the company — a ₹1 crore round selling ~3%, fourteen months after incorporation, from unnamed anchor investors, is angel money dressed as an institutional seed, so even the floor of the seed benchmark row may sit above what they actually pay; a ₹3L offer here would not be an anomaly. (2) Every operating claim is company-issued and unaudited: the ₹6.30 crore GMV, the 25x growth and the eight-country footprint all trace to an ANI-syndicated advertorial (The Tribune carries an explicit no-responsibility disclaimer), a StartupTalky piece, and a Dealroom page that now 404s. No independent journalism exists. If the GMV figure is soft, the trade-operations role in particular does not exist. (3) The metro benchmark tier may be wrong — New Palam Vihar is fringe Gurugram and there is a Panipat office; if hiring lands there, subtract 15-30% from every band. (4) Headcount is unverified: LinkedIn self-declares 11-50 but surfaces four employee profiles, and if the real number is closer to eight, they are hiring one or two people total, not five. (5) The profile was deliberately left unverified, which is why band_confidence is dropped a step to low. Separately, do not merge this with "Baba", the US patient-advocacy startup that raised $6.5M led by General Catalyst in February 2026 — different company, different continent.

estimated_roles.title: Territory Sales Manager
estimated_roles.family: Field and channel sales (dealer-facing)
estimated_roles.why: Listed twice on the careers page and it is the seat the round most directly funds - taking the dealer/service network from ~150 touchpoints to a stated 250 by FY28 needs territory feet on the ground. Honest caveat: at an auto OEM this title normally wants 3-6 years of 2W/3W dealer sales, so a 2026/27 fresher almost never gets the 'Manager' badge on day one. companies.fit_reason:
OSM will hire 2026/27 graduates, but mostly not into the roles a business-track candidate is imagining. All five live listings are mid-to-senior - an AGM/DGM/GM, an Assistant Manager/Sr. EHS Officer, two Territory Sales Managers and an Area Sales Manager - and none is a 0-1 year requisition. There is no named management trainee or graduate leadership programme, which is what a 350-700 person manufacturer would need for structured fresher intake; at this size, junior hiring is requisition-by-requisition through Naukri and referrals.

What genuinely works in a fresher's favour: the round funds dealer network expansion from ~150 to 250 touchpoints by FY28, and that is manpower-hungry, junior-heavy work - dealer onboarding, field sales support, service desks - that OEMs staff with fresh graduates because the volume is high and the pay is low. A mechanical or electrical graduate also has a clean shot at plant-side sourcing and service seats. What works against: this is a plant-heavy engineering business where the prestige track is GET/technical, not business; the business-track pay is manufacturer-grade Rs 3.5-6L, roughly half what a funded consumer-tech firm pays a business associate in Gurugram; the work is travel-intensive and tier-2/3 based; and anyone hoping for product, growth, category or analytics work will not find it - OSM has no such function at fresher level. Rated mixed rather than good because the doors that exist are narrow and low-paid, and mixed rather than poor because unlike a bank NBFC or a 30-year-old industrial house, OSM has a concrete, funded, headcount-creating expansion underway right now.
companies.caveat: Four honest reasons this could be wrong. (1) The careers page is stale - its five posts are dated July 2024, so it both understates real hiring and gives me no live fresher requisition to anchor on; every predicted role here is inferred from the stated use of funds and the business model, not observed. LinkedIn and Naukri reportedly carry more live requisitions than the site, and those would be the real evidence. (2) There is no auto-OEM or manufacturing row anywhere in the benchmark file - the closest anchors are consumer-internet field sales (IndiaMART, Delhivery, BYJU'S) and BPO/manufacturing MT programmes, so every band here is a cross-family transfer, which is why I dropped confidence to low. (3) The stage label is contested and it cuts both ways: reading OSM as a funded Series C+ startup would push these bands up by Rs 2-4L, reading it as a mid-size private manufacturer would push them down by Rs 0.5-1L, and I chose the latter on the profile's own advice. (4) The largest single risk is employment structure, not level: OEMs routinely push territory sales and service headcount onto dealer payrolls rather than their own, where a comparable seat pays Rs 2.5-4L with no OEM benefits. If OSM staffs its 100 new touchpoints that way - which is the cheap and common path - real fresher pay lands a full band below these numbers and the OSM name does not appear on the offer letter at all.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the mix cuts in both directions. In favour: the work genuinely is fresher work. Marketplace catalogue and ads operations, performance-marketing execution, social content and production follow-up are roles Indian D2C brands fill with 0-1 year graduates as a matter of course, the company has real revenue (~Rs 1 crore/month) so a hire is not paid out of runway alone, the round explicitly names "team expansion", and at a sub-30-person brand a fresher sits next to the founders and owns a P&L lever within months — unusually good learning per rupee. Against: the pay is Rs 3-6 LPA for most of these seats, which is below what a 2026/2027 engineering graduate with a campus offer would take; there is no careers page, no ATS, no HR function and zero published openings today, so entry is entirely through a cold LinkedIn message to Ankit Dass or Vidushi Chaudhary rather than any process a campus placement cell can plug into; a large share of the declared headcount is factory labour, not office roles, so the actual office hiring volume this year may be three to six people total; and an engineering degree buys almost nothing here — a footwear brand values Excel, marketplace panels, Meta Ads Manager and merchandising sense, so the graduate competes against commerce and fashion-tech backgrounds with no technical premium. Worth applying to only if the candidate specifically wants consumer-brand operating experience; a poor fit for someone optimising for salary, structure or a technical career track.

companies.fit_reason:
Mixed, and the split is sharp rather than blurry — this company has two hiring engines and only one of them is open to an engineering graduate.

The engine that does the volume hiring is clinical. Roughly 350-400 of its people are therapists spread across 90+ centres, and the recurring vacancies are Therapy Specialist, Rehabilitation Therapist and Behaviour Therapist. Those require BASLP, occupational-therapy, psychology or RCI-registered credentials and ABA training. A 2026/2027 BE/BTech graduate cannot enter that track at all, which removes most of the company's headcount from consideration in one stroke.

The engine that is open is small. The Thane head-office cluster — product, content, social media, marketing, finance, central ops — is likely well under 100 people out of a 350-500 total, and the currently posted head-office roles skew to titles that want 2-4 years (Social Media Manager, Product Manager, Content Writer). The genuinely fresher-shaped openings on the current list are Associate Content Writer and a Video Editor internship, both of which pay poorly.

What lifts this from poor to mixed is what the round funds. All three stated uses create entry-level business work: expanding the centre network into new states needs centre-launch and centre-ops associates in cities like Vijayawada and Aurangabad; commercialising the Get SET Early eye-tracking screener through hospitals and paediatricians needs a real B2B field/inside-sales motion the company does not visibly have yet; and a 90-centre parent-enquiry funnel needs performance-marketing and admissions-counsellor headcount that turns over constantly. The hiring pattern already matches — a receptionist in Aurangabad and a therapy specialist in Vijayawada, both outside Maharashtra, alongside the Thane product/content cluster.

The honest caveats for a graduate weighing this. Pay is materially below what the same effort buys at a Mumbai tech startup; several of the realistic entry lanes (counsellor, centre ops, front desk) are lower-ceiling operational jobs rather than analyst tracks; a lot of the work is in-person and centre-facing, sometimes outside Maharashtra; and an engineering degree carries no premium in a therapy chain — the differentiators are comfort talking to anxious parents, willingness to travel, and in the BD case the ability to sit across from paediatricians and hospital procurement. Where the engineering background genuinely helps is the technology-platform and Get SET Early product side, which is exactly where the openings are thinnest and the titles most senior.
companies.caveat:
The most likely way this is wrong is the role list itself. The company's own careers page is an unfinished template — a form plus a "Roles we offer" heading filled with lorem ipsum — so every "listed now" title here came from LinkedIn Jobs and SimplyHired aggregation, and two of those postings are about a month old. Aggregators retain filled and expired listings, and Naukri and Indeed both returned 403 so nothing could be cross-checked. Treat the "listed now" roles as "posted recently", not "confirmed open on 10 Sep 2026".

Second, the sector discount is my judgement, not a sourced cut. No benchmark row in the file measures paediatric-healthcare-services pay; I inferred the 0.6-0.75x from the notes' own language about consumer/D2C companies paying closer to the seed row. If Butterfly Learnings actually pays its Thane head-office cluster like a Mumbai tech startup — plausible, since the round explicitly funds a technology platform and AI capability, and the Product Manager seat may sit close to the tech team — every band here is 20-30% too low. If instead it pays like a suburban clinic chain, the content and ops bands could be another notch lower still.

Third, the city-tier call is a coin-flip that moves the numbers materially. I treated Thane as Mumbai metro; Entrackr and Inc42 report the HQ as "Mumbai" while LinkedIn and the registered address say Thane. Had I used the benchmark's "other Indian city" rows instead, most bands would drop roughly 25%.

Fourth, the stage label in the export is wrong in a way that cuts against the bands being too high, not too low: this was a pre-Series B, and the real Series A was ₹32 Cr in April 2024. The Series A-B row is still the right row, but the company is at the earlier, thinner end of it — ₹15.5 Cr revenue is small for that row's implied company.

Finally, no band here is published by the company. These are benchmark-derived estimates, and at a sub-100-person head office individual offers vary more than any band.
