estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office / Business Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate - entry-level (0-2 years), India
estimated_roles.why: Two founders, a first institutional round, and a stated 12-month commercial target is the classic trigger for a founder's-office hire who chases cohort/retention numbers, investor reporting and whatever is on fire that week. Marked 'possible' rather than 'likely' because at a $1.2M round this seat often stays unfilled or goes to an intern, and when it is filled it is usually a tier-1 campus hire.

estimated_roles.title: Customer Experience Associate (parent support and warranty)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (support sub-band; no dedicated support row in the benchmarks)
estimated_roles.why: A screen-free device in the hands of a 4-10 year old generates setup calls, pairing problems, damaged-card replacements and warranty claims from anxious parents. As units ship at scale this stops being something the founders answer on WhatsApp. Lowest-paid seat on this list and the least career-forming for an engineering graduate, so it is listed for completeness, not as a recommendation.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the reason is a timing mismatch rather than a policy against freshers. What works: a 26-person seed D2C brand in Bengaluru that just raised for demand generation and fulfilment genuinely does hire cheap junior execution - someone to run the ad accounts, load the catalogue, pack and track the boxes, answer the parents. Those are real entry-level seats and the money for them is in the round. What does not work: every one of the six roles open today is a lead, head or manager title - Creative and Content Lead, Ecommerce Manager, Product Growth Manager (D2C), Head of Marketing, Head of Digital Marketing, Warehouse Manager. Not one is entry-level, so a 2026/2027 graduate applying this week has nothing to apply to on the business track. The junior seats above are the layer that gets hired three to six months after those leads land, which points at late 2026 into 2027 rather than now. Two further frictions for an engineering graduate specifically. First, these business roles are contested by commerce, communications and BBA graduates who look more natural on paper for catalogue, content and support work; the fulfilment/supply-chain seat is the one where an engineering degree reads as an asset. Second, Wippi is hiring engineers directly - Embedded Software Engineer (listed twice) and a Testing & Quality Engineer Intern - so an engineering graduate's highest-probability route into this company is the technical track, not the business track. A practical note: there is no careers page on wippi.com and no structured graduate programme at 26 people, so entry-level hiring here happens through the founders' networks, LinkedIn DMs and internships that convert. A cold application to a job board is the weakest available channel.
companies.caveat: The honest reason this could be wrong: no role on this list is actually posted. Every one of the six roles Wippi has live is a lead or manager title, so all six bands here are predictions about a hiring layer that does not exist yet, priced off benchmark rows that no source tags by funding stage - the seed-stage cut in every row I used is the benchmark author's inference from company names, not observed seed offers. Three specific ways this breaks. First, a 26-person hardware company may simply never open these seats: the standard move at $1.2M is to hire one experienced generalist who does catalogue, ads and fulfilment together, or to outsource the whole layer to a D2C growth agency and a 3PL, in which case the correct answer for a fresher is zero roles rather than six. Second, the confidence rating is low for a reason - the category, ops and business-analyst rows are all self-described as low-confidence extrapolations, and I lowered a step further for headcount, so individual offers here will vary more than these bands do; a founder who wants a specific person will pay outside them in either direction. Third, four of the six live roles came from an aggregator mirror rather than LinkedIn directly and may already be filled, which would change what the junior layer under them looks like. One more thing worth knowing before any conversation with them: wippi.com advertises '59,000+ families' while the funding coverage frames 15,000 families as a forward target - those cannot both be current customers, so do not quote either figure back to them as traction, and read the site number as marketing reach.

estimated_roles.title: Zone / City Operations Executive (fleet and hub ops)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: The round's headline use of funds is quadrupling the active fleet to 200,000 EVs in two years and building out service hubs and battery-swapping infrastructure. That is a people-heavy ground operation: every new hub needs someone running vehicle uptime, battery rotation, redeployment and mechanic scheduling. This is the single largest entry-level hiring pool at Yulu by volume — but it is recruited through blue-collar channels (Apna, Jobhai, recruitment.yulu.bike walk-in drives), not the corporate careers board, which is why zero such roles appear in the profile's live-listing check.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Fleet Planning Analyst (central ops)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Going from ~50k to 200k vehicles plus a battery-swap network is a planning problem before it is a headcount problem: demand forecasting by zone, spares and battery inventory, hub siting, utilisation-per-vehicle economics. This is the central-ops ladder (as opposed to the hub ladder) and it is the one genuinely fresher-friendly, decently-paid business seat an engineering graduate can realistically target here. Yulu Express, the new higher-payload logistics scooter, adds a second fleet to plan for.

estimated_roles.title: Enterprise Partnerships / B2B Accounts Associate
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: The round explicitly funds deepening enterprise partnerships with quick-commerce, food-delivery and last-mile logistics platforms, and Yulu Express is aimed squarely at e-commerce logistics, bike taxis and express parcel. Someone junior has to sit under the partnership leads doing fleet-allocation coordination, per-account utilisation reporting, onboarding of rider cohorts and QBR prep. Note this is a field/account-servicing role at a mobility operator, not a SaaS SDR seat — priced accordingly.

estimated_roles.title: Business Analyst / Data Analyst (Business)
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: A per-minute rental business with a physical fleet lives on unit economics: revenue per vehicle per day, idle time, battery-swap cost per km, hub P&L, churn on monthly subscriptions. IPO positioning sharpens the need for clean reporting. Marked possible rather than likely because Yulu's only live analytical requisition is a Data Scientist filed under its Engineering stream, which suggests it staffs this need technically rather than through a business-analyst ladder.

estimated_roles.title: Growth / Performance Marketing Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: Quadrupling supply only pays off if demand follows in each new zone, so app-install campaigns, city-level launch marketing, retention/subscription funnels and rider-acquisition creative all scale with the fleet. Possible rather than likely because a hardware-and-hubs company spends its incremental capital on assets, not CAC, and a marketing team of this size typically adds one such person a year, not a cohort.

estimated_roles.title: Associate - Founder's Office / Strategy
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Several outlets frame the round as balance-sheet preparation ahead of an IPO, and the debt leg (~$30M of the $93M) plus the separate Yuma Energy battery entity mean real corporate-structuring and investor-reporting work. Companies in this position routinely open one or two founder's-office seats for sharp graduates. Possible, not likely: it is a one-or-two-headcount function and often filled by an ex-consulting or tier-1 MBA hire rather than a fresh engineering graduate.

companies.fit_reason: Real hiring demand exists and the round guarantees more of it, but it is badly split against a 2026/27 engineering graduate's expectations. The volume is in field and hub operations at Rs 3-5 LPA — genuine jobs, created directly by the fleet quadrupling, but recruited through blue-collar channels (Apna, Jobhai, walk-in drives at recruitment.yulu.bike) rather than the corporate careers board, and paid at a level most engineering graduates will not accept. The well-paid central seats (fleet planning, analytics, partnerships, founder's office) are real but few — this is a ~760-person company whose headcount grew ~3% YoY, so these are one-or-two-headcount openings a year that compete against tier-1 MBAs and 1-3 year experienced hires. Meanwhile the corporate board today carries exactly two requisitions, both Bengaluru, both approved a week after the round, and both senior/technical (Senior Product Designer, Data Scientist) — nothing an entry-level business candidate can apply to right now. Not "poor": Yulu does hire business-side graduates and the capital is committed to expansion. Not "good": the path in for a fresher is either a low-paid ops role or a narrow, competitive central seat, and neither is currently posted.
companies.caveat: These are estimates derived from benchmark rows, not published bands — Yulu has never disclosed compensation for any of these roles, and none of the six roles above is currently posted. Every role is a prediction tied to the round's stated uses of funds (fleet quadrupling to 200k EVs, service hubs and battery-swap infrastructure, enterprise partnerships with quick-commerce and delivery platforms, the Yulu Express logistics scooter, IPO preparation), not an observed opening. Two data caveats carried over from the profile: (1) the Rs 601 Cr figure in the source export does not match reporting, which puts the round at $93M total ($63M equity + ~$30M debt, roughly Rs 815 Cr all-in or ~Rs 550 Cr for the equity leg) — the export figure looks like the equity portion at a stale FX rate; (2) the live-listing check ran against the MyNextHire board embedded in Yulu's careers page and returned only two requisitions, and LinkedIn could not be read from this environment to cross-check, so the absence of posted business roles is a strong signal but not an exhaustive one. Field-ops pay in particular varies by city and by how much of the package is monthly incentive rather than fixed CTC.

estimated_roles.title: Generalist, Founding Team
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate (entry-level, 0-2 yrs)
estimated_roles.why: Live on the careers page (Gurugram) as an open application rather than a defined seat. At a ~1-month-old forward-deployed firm this is the only listed door a 0-1 yr graduate can realistically walk through: undefined scope, sitting next to the founders, doing whatever the first enterprise deployments need — customer research, deployment tracking, recruiting ops, data pulls. Ties directly to what the round funds, since the seed is a hiring round to stand up the delivery organisation.

estimated_roles.title: AI Deployment Strategist
estimated_roles.family: Product analyst / APM-adjacent client-facing strategy (entry-level edge of the band)
estimated_roles.why: Live on the careers page, Department: Strategy, Gurugram. Client-facing and roadmap-shaping — mapping a BFSI/healthcare/manufacturing customer's workflow onto agents the forward-deployed engineers then build. Honest caveat: this reads as a 2-5 year hire wanting real technical depth, so a 2026/2027 graduate is a stretch candidate who would land at the bottom of the range, if at all. Included because it is the only other listed non-engineering seat and the title must be quoted exactly.

estimated_roles.title: Deployment Analyst (AI agent delivery and evaluation)
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst (entry-level, 0-2 yrs)
estimated_roles.why: Predicted, not listed. The round funds ~50 forward-deployed engineers in month one, and the model they are productising is a Cars24 voice agent handling 1M+ conversation minutes a month. That volume generates continuous non-engineering work — transcript review, agent quality and eval scoring, workflow and exception mapping, customer-facing delivery reporting — which is the standard place services firms park sharp graduates so engineers stay on build. Cheapest headcount that makes a delivery org scale.

estimated_roles.title: Business Development Representative, Enterprise GTM
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management (entry-level, 0-2 yrs)
estimated_roles.why: Predicted, not listed. The seed explicitly funds go-to-market hires, and an Account Director, GTM is already open. Enterprise BFSI/healthcare/manufacturing/logistics outbound needs pipeline research and sequencing under that director. Marked possible rather than likely because at 10-50 people a first Account Director usually carries their own bag for two to three quarters before an SDR seat is created, and the reporting broke out no marketing or demand-gen allocation at all.

companies.fit_reason: There is one genuine door and no graduate programme behind it. Of the five live listings, two are engineering (Forward Deployed Engineer, FDE Engineering Manager) and are out of scope; Account Director, GTM is a senior bag-carrying seat closed to a 0-1 yr graduate; AI Deployment Strategist is client-facing and technical and reads as a 2-5 year hire. That leaves "Generalist, Founding Team", which is an open application rather than a defined seat — a fresher can apply, but the bar is exceptional-only and there is no structured intake, no campus process, and no cohort to be hired into. Not "poor", because the round is explicitly a hiring round and a services firm whose product is people will keep opening seats as delivery scales, and forward-deployed delivery genuinely does absorb sharp analysts. Not "good", because the company is roughly one month old at ~10-50 people, is staffing a founding team from senior networks (Cars24 AI, xAI, Zomato, Atlassian), and at this size will almost always take a second-jobber over a graduate for the same seat. Two further things a candidate should weigh: the business is a single-customer, single-investor operation today, so job security tracks one commercial relationship rather than a diversified book; and at a forward-deployed firm the line between business and engineering roles is blurry, so a graduate without technical depth will find the non-engineering seats narrower than the headcount plan suggests. Best realistic route in is the Generalist open application, or waiting one to two quarters for the delivery-analyst layer to appear once the first non-Cars24 accounts land.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not published pay. Deployment Inc has published no salary band, no headcount, and no entry-level hiring plan; the company is about one month old, so there is no Glassdoor, AmbitionBox or 6figr history to check any of this against — the underlying benchmark rows themselves are confidence low-to-medium and are extrapolated from live postings at comparable seed companies, not from observed offers at this employer. Confidence was lowered one step from those rows for company size and stage ambiguity: at 10-50 people, pay is founder-set rather than market-set and a single decision can move an offer several lakh in either direction, and this is a corporate-launched spinout with unicorn cash and anchor revenue rather than a normal independent seed, which pulls it toward Series-A behaviour in ways the seed rows do not capture. Two of the four roles below are predictions with no posting behind them. The two that are listed are quoted verbatim from the careers page as read on 2026-09-10 — a page at a one-month-old company that will change fast, so re-check it before acting. Note also that "Deployment" is an ordinary English word: name-only searching returns Kubernetes and Office documentation, and the company was only pinned down by pairing the name with the Cars24 investor field, so any figure attributed to "Deployment" from a general search should be treated as a different entity until proven otherwise. Finally, headcount could not be verified against LinkedIn or any company statement; the 10-50 range is an estimate derived from launch reporting of a ~50-engineer first-month hiring intent.

It is a restaurant floor service seat, though: greeting, order-taking, table and takeaway flow, complaint handling and delivery-order coordination. An engineering graduate can be hired into it but the degree buys nothing, and progression is toward Captain and Assistant Outlet Manager rather than toward any analytical track.

estimated_roles.family: Outlet operations / hospitality management
estimated_roles.why: Listed now in both Mumbai (posted 2026-09-06 and 2026-06-19) and Delhi/New Delhi (2026-08-10, 2026-06-23) - the repeated Delhi postings are the clearest signal that the expansion the round funds is already being staffed. The job is P&L-adjacent floor management: shift rosters, inventory and wastage, food-cost control, aggregator ratings, hygiene audits. Realistically filled by an IHM/hotel-management graduate with 2-4 years of QSR floor time, so a 0-1 year engineering graduate would be a stretch hire at the bottom of the band, if at all.

estimated_roles.title: Outlet Expansion / New Store Launch Associate
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Directly tied to what the round funds - expanding the outlet network beyond Mumbai, with Delhi hiring already live. Multi-city rollout at 3-to-N outlets needs someone junior doing site shortlisting, landlord and vendor coordination, fit-out tracking, licence and FSSAI paperwork and launch-week checklists. This is the classic city-launch seat and the one place an engineering graduate's spreadsheet and project-tracking habits genuinely earn their pay. Not currently listed, and at this size it may be one hire or none.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Central Kitchen Associate
estimated_roles.family: Operations and supply chain
estimated_roles.why: Supply-chain strengthening is named in the reporting as a use of proceeds, and a dosa chain going multi-city has to move from per-outlet purchasing to a central kitchen and commissary model - batter and chutney production planning, cold-chain to outlets, vendor rate contracts, wastage and yield tracking. Genuinely quantitative work, but priced on food-service supply-chain scales (the benchmark's own anchor for entry supply-chain analysts at startups is Rs 3-5L), not on quick-commerce scales.

estimated_roles.title: Growth / Delivery Channel Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: A QSR at this stage lives on Swiggy and Zomato: listing and menu optimisation, discount and ad-spend management on the aggregator panels, ratings and review response, plus Instagram-led brand marketing for a Bandra-born food brand. Guest-experience investment is named in the round coverage and this is where a marketing hire would sit. Adjusted below the growth benchmark because aggregator channel management at a three-outlet chain is a narrower job than performance marketing at a funded consumer-tech company.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office / Business Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: The best-fit seat for an engineering graduate here, and the only one where the degree is an actual advantage: unit-economics modelling per outlet, cohort and daypart sales analysis, investor reporting to Claypond and the co-investors, and running the operational/tech capability workstream the round is meant to fund. companies.fit_reason: Poor, and I would advise a 2026/2027 engineering graduate against targeting this company for a business-track first job. Every one of the ten open roles is a hospitality or back-office seat, and none is an engineering-adjacent business role: Guest Experience Associate and Captain are restaurant floor service jobs recruited from IHM/hotel-management and QSR service pools; Assistant Outlet Manager wants prior outlet floor experience; Junior Accountant wants B.Com/CA-inter; Welfare Manager and Senior Manager - Head of People are experienced HR hires. There are no engineering postings at all, which is exactly what you would expect from a three-outlet dosa chain. The structural problem is scale: with roughly 60-150 people of whom nearly all are outlet kitchen and floor staff across ~3 outlets, the Mumbai head office is a handful of desks, so the graduate-shaped seats (founder's office, expansion analyst, supply chain, delivery-channel growth) exist as zero or one openings a year and, when they open, go to someone with food-service or MBA background as often as to a fresh engineer. The honest read: an engineering graduate who genuinely wants restaurant operations could get real ownership fast here — a Rs 35 Cr raise and a live Delhi push means someone junior will be handed a new-city rollout — but the pay is hospitality-scale, the technical degree is not what is being bought, and the realistic entry is through an unadvertised founder's-office or expansion seat via direct outreach to the founders, not through a listed opening.
companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. Benne has published no salary band, and neither has any comparable early-stage Indian QSR chain. Three specific weaknesses: the underlying ops benchmark row is itself marked low confidence and is built from tech-startup rather than restaurant comparables, so my QSR haircut is judgement, not measurement; the round label is contested (export says Seed, press and the RoC filing say Pre-Series A) though the business is early-stage either way; and the live role list comes from the LinkedIn jobs tab, where postings from as recently as three days ago already show "no longer accepting applications" to logged-out viewers, so some June/July listings may be filled. Every predicted role is inference from what the round funds (Delhi and multi-city outlet expansion, supply chain, guest experience) — none is confirmed to exist, and at ~3 outlets the head office may simply not add a graduate seat this year. Revenue and headcount inputs are company-reported and unaudited. Name-collision risk is real: "benne" is Kannada for butter and several unrelated dosa outlets and a separate "Benne Room" post similar hospitality roles.

estimated_roles.title: Claims / FWA Analyst (Fraud, Waste and Abuse Analyst)

A foundational FWA model — the round's stated 'core focus' — needs humans reviewing flagged claims, labelling and adjudicating training data, tuning rule libraries, and doing false-positive QA against insurer and TPA feedback. That is entry-level, domain-heavy, desk-based work an engineering graduate can do with SQL and Excel. Caveat on competition: Indian claims-review teams are often staffed with BAMS/BDS/pharmacy/nursing graduates and certified medical coders rather than engineers, which both widens the applicant pool and drags the pay floor down.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the near-term reading is worse than the medium-term one. Right now the company has four published openings and three are data science (Data Scientist, Lead Data Scientist, Sr. Manager Data Scientist) — technical, not entry-level. The single non-engineering req, Key Account Manager, asks for 5-10 years with an MBA preferred and insurance-domain pre-sales experience, so as of today there is no business-track seat a 0-1 year graduate can apply to. That is the honest answer to "can I get in now": not through the careers page. What keeps this from being "poor" is the shape of the business and of the round. Claims-fraud AI is a labelling- and review-intensive product: somebody has to adjudicate flagged claims, build and tune FWA rule libraries, QA document-extraction output and run UAT at each insurer, and that work is genuinely juniorable — a foundational FWA model, named as the core focus of the raise, makes it more juniorable, not less, because model training needs annotated ground truth at volume. Enterprise delivery capability is a second named use of funds and is the classic place a 79-person company adds 0-2 year analysts. Two structural headwinds to price in: enterprise insurance sales rewards domain credibility, so commercial hiring here skews to people with insurer/TPA backgrounds rather than fresh graduates; and the claims-analyst seats compete with medical and paramedical graduates and certified coders, who are the conventional hire for that work in India. Realistic play for an engineering graduate: target the analyst and delivery seats rather than the commercial ones, apply speculatively rather than waiting for a listing, and lead with SQL, Python and any healthcare-claims or insurance exposure.
companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. Consint.AI has published no salary band, and neither has any company in this dataset — treat every figure as a planning prior, not an offer. Specific weaknesses to hold in mind: (1) Five of the six roles below are PREDICTED, not posted; only Key Account Manager exists today, and its spec (5-10 years, MBA preferred) puts it out of reach for a 2026/27 fresher, so the band shown against it prices a junior seat the company has not yet opened. (2) Every Noida band rests on "Series A-B / other Indian city" benchmark rows that the source file itself marks low confidence and describes as extrapolated — no reachable dataset segments Indian pay by funding stage and non-metro city, and Noida is an awkward fit for either city tier. (3) Band confidence was lowered one step from the rows' own ratings because the company is small (~79 LinkedIn-derived employees, an estimate, not an audited figure) and the round is small in absolute terms. (4) The company profile itself carries a process caveat: funding details are the company's own press release, not independently triangulated across trade press, because the research session's web-search budget was exhausted. (5) Its own site is internally inconsistent — the Key Account Manager listing card says Noida while the job page and Preferred Location field say Mumbai, and the role is oddly tagged Job Function "Development" / Department "Support" — so treat location and function tags on any future posting with suspicion and confirm at application. (6) Openings change; check https://consint.ai/careers/ directly rather than relying on this snapshot dated 10 Sep 2026.

companies.fit_reason: Four things stack against a 2026/27 engineering graduate. First, there is no hiring signal at all: the careers page loaded and says there are no open positions, directing enquiries to hr@vasukiindia.com. Second, the firm is roughly 7-15 people with six named staff plus the founder, and it already has the one entry seat it needs filled (Sahil Patel, Junior Analyst) — a team this size adds a fresher every couple of years at best, and each hire is a real cost against the management fee. Third, the Rs 100 Cr that put this company in the dataset is investable fund corpus, not operating capital, so unlike a genuine Series A it creates zero hiring budget; the firm's own revenue is a management fee on AUM, which grows in single-digit crores, not in headcount steps. Fourth, and most decisive, the entry roles that do exist here are credential-gated in a way engineering degrees do not satisfy: buy-side research and fund operations in Mumbai screen for CFA Level 1/2, CA, or an MBA in finance, and an engineering graduate competes against candidates who already hold those. The one genuine engineering edge — Python, data pipelines, backtesting for a quant or portfolio-analytics seat — is exactly the function a seven-person discretionary equity shop outsources or does in Excel. A graduate wanting buy-side exposure is better served targeting larger AMCs, broker research desks with structured analyst programmes, or fintech firms that actually run graduate intakes; a cold mail to hr@vasukiindia.com is a lottery ticket, not a pipeline.
companies.caveat: These are estimates derived from benchmark rows, not published bands — Vasuki India has published no salary information at all. Three specific weaknesses: (a) the round row is misclassified, so the "Series A" stage input that would normally drive the band is unusable and I substituted a judgement call; (b) no benchmark family in the file covers boutique asset management, PMS or AIF, so every band here is a startup comparable bent toward financial services rather than a financial-services observation; (c) the careers page is a real, loaded zero ("We currently do not have any open positions"), so all four roles are predictions with nothing listed to anchor them — in any given year this firm plausibly opens none of them. Headcount (7-15) is estimated from the team page only and could not be cross-checked on LinkedIn. Do not confuse this firm with the unrelated "Vasuki AI" commodity-hedging startup, or with the separate vasuki-india.com domain.

companies.fit_reason: Hulp does hire freshers at volume, but mostly into work that does not use an engineering degree. The company is roughly 30-50 people and the bulk of that is the personal-assistant and coordination roster - StartupFox describes a 50-member operations team - so the realistic entry point for a 2026/27 graduate is a pod PA or a vertical ops associate at Rs 3-5.5L, competing against hospitality, BPO and generalist-graduate applicants, with rostered hours and evening/weekend member coverage. That is a legitimate first job and it scales with the funded metro expansion, but it is a service-delivery career track, not an analytics or product one. The seats an engineering grad would actually want - founder's office / city launch, ops analyst, growth - probably number one to three across the whole company today, and Inc42 reports the round's explicit hiring intent is "hire senior leaders", not junior volume. Two things do push in the fresher's favour: the founders are credible operators (ex-Policybazaar CBO, ex-Mitgo India MD) so a founder's-office seat here is genuinely good learning, and a five-city expansion over two years mechanically creates city-launch work that early juniors get handed. Net: apply, but treat it as an ops-first company and check which track you are being hired into before signing.

companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates, not published bands - Hulp has disclosed no salary figure for any role. Three specific weaknesses: (1) the primary benchmark row is itself marked low confidence and is triangulated, not measured; (2) I could not verify a single live opening today - the one public posting (Meal Management Associate, Gurugram) already shows "no longer accepting applications", and Hulp has no careers page at all, so every role below except that title is a prediction from the business model and the round's stated use of funds, not from a posting; (3) the service-delivery down-adjustment on the two ops roles is my judgment call, not a sourced cut - if Hulp positions PA pods as a premium white-collar career track rather than a concierge roster, the real numbers could sit Rs 1-1.5L above my band. Anyone tracking this should watch linkedin.com/company/hulpin rather than a careers URL; a company this size hires in bursts and can go from zero to several openings within weeks.

companies.fit_reason: Expect ESOP on any offer here — Series A, ~$27M raised, founded 2024, roughly a dozen people, so grants are early and the percentage is unusually large by later-stage standards. Treat it as paper, not pay. Three specifics for a fresher: (a) a Rs 1-3 LPA notional on top of fixed is a realistic order of magnitude for an entry business seat at this size, which is why the benchmark rows' "total high" sits only ~3 LPA above "fixed high"; (b) liquidity is remote — a 2024-founded reinsurer building regulatory capital is on a long horizon, and there is no secondary market for this; (c) a slice of the round is regulatory capital for EarthRe rather than growth spend, which means cash comp discipline is likelier here than at a pure-software Series A. Ask for the strike price, the total outstanding share count (not just your option count), the vesting schedule and cliff, and the exercise window after leaving. Negotiate the fixed number as if the ESOP were zero.
companies.caveat: Mixed, and worth being precise about why rather than rounding to good or poor. The positive: exactly one non-engineering role is live, "Quantitative Analyst – Parametric Insurance", and its structure — Ahmedabad, office-based, full-time but starting as a 3-month internship — is a genuine fresher on-ramp, not a disguised senior req. A 2026/2027 engineering graduate with strong statistics, Python and an interest in climate or catastrophe data is a real candidate for it today. The round is also explicitly earmarked for actuarial, underwriting and cat-modelling headcount, so the non-engineering surface should widen over the next few months. The negatives are structural: at ~11 people the total number of business-track graduate seats across the whole year is likely low single digits, so this is a one-role application, not a campus pipeline; the strongest-paying predicted roles (actuarial, underwriting) usually want cleared IFoA/IAI exams or prior insurance exposure, which most engineering grads will not have on day one; there is no graduate programme, no structured training and no cohort, so learning is entirely apprenticeship off two or three senior people; and the location constrains it — Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar office-based, which is a relocation for most candidates and a thinner market to exit into than Bengaluru. Also note the aggregator noise: Naukri and Jobaaj surface a "Finance Associate" and claim 3-5 openings, but that role is not on the official careers page and should be treated as stale.

companies.fit_reason: Real entry opportunity exists, but almost none of it is on the careers page and most of it pays badly. Of the five live roles, two are Country Leads (senior, expat/regional-hire level) and three are state Program Managers that read as 3-5 year agri-development hires — none is a graduate seat, and all three PM postings have been open since 24 Dec 2025, suggesting evergreen field recruitment rather than urgent vacancies. The company's real graduate rung is the field associate layer beneath those Program Managers: genuine, high-volume, likely to grow as the round funds deeper India coverage, but rural-posted at ₹3-4.5L, which is below what most 2026/27 engineering graduates will accept. The one attractive fresher seat — MRV/carbon analyst on the GeoAI data side in Bengaluru — is real but scarce, because the desk-based org is only 11-50 people and the 150 headcount figure is field staff, not corporate seats. Worth noting for a technical graduate: there are currently zero engineering roles open at a company that just raised specifically to scale a satellite-AI platform, so do not assume a technical path opens up soon. Good fit if you want climate/agri field impact and can accept development-sector pay; poor fit if you want a Bengaluru tech-startup package.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not published bands — Mitti Labs has never disclosed compensation, and nothing here came from the company. Confidence is low and deliberately so: the non-metro Series A-B rows I leaned on hardest are flagged "low / extrapolated" in the benchmark file itself (no source segments Indian salaries by funding stage and non-metro city), the desk-based org is tiny (11-50 on LinkedIn versus a company-stated 150 that is mostly field staff), and I applied two judgement-based discounts — agri-development field scale and non-SaaS revenue — that no source quantifies precisely for this sector. companies.fit_reason:
Mixed, and the mix matters more than the average. On the positive side: this is a genuinely hiring-shaped company — funded twice in twelve months, claiming 8x growth, about to open new cities — and multi-city expansion in quick commerce is one of the few things in India that reliably absorbs raw graduates into real ownership fast. A 0-1 yr engineering grad who wants operating experience over a title can get a city launch or supply-chain seat here that would take three years to reach at a larger firm.

Against it: three real problems. (1) There is no way in. No careers page exists — I confirmed the full sitemap has no careers section, no ATS tenant exists on Lever/Greenhouse/Workable/Keka/Darwinbox/Zoho, no LinkedIn company page exists, and LinkedIn's public jobs API returns zero HomeRun postings in Bengaluru. (2) The volume of openings is skewed to the bottom of the pay range: at a 60-minute SLA across 76 pin codes, most seats are hub-ops and field-sales roles at ₹3.2-6L, which is well under what an engineering campus treats as a floor. The ₹8-11L seats — founder's office, city launch, supply-chain analyst — are one or two headcount each and frequently go to MBAs or to someone the founder already knows. (3) Only ~11 employees are verifiable and no careers page exists, so nothing about the hiring plan is confirmed; no hiring intent was mentioned in any of the funding coverage.

Verdict: worth a direct outbound approach for the expansion, category or supply-chain seats specifically. Do not wait for a job post — there will not be one. And go in knowing which half of the ops band the seat sits in before discussing numbers.

companies.fit_reason: Raydean does hire fresh engineering graduates, but overwhelmingly onto the engineering track — GET/production, QA, design and drafting for structures and towers — not into business roles. The business-side entry seats listed above are real and reasonably predictable from the business model, yet they share three problems for a 2026/27 grad. First, none of them are advertised: the careers page's entire openings module is unmigrated lorem-ipsum theme demo content ("Senior Business Manager1", Kolkata, Full Time), so the site gives literally no hiring signal, and the only genuine vacancy found anywhere is an Area Sales Manager at 5-10 yrs experience, which a fresher cannot apply to. Second, the round does not fund headcount: proceeds go to a consolidated manufacturing campus with in-house galvanization and automated lines, and MD Samarth Dakshini's framing was about integration, not team-building — so do not expect a hiring wave off the back of it. Third, the pay is genuinely low. A Jaipur manufacturing business-track offer at 3-5 LPA is roughly a third to half of what the same graduate would see at a metro tech employer, and per Naukri JobSpeak 2026 only 40 pct of Indian undergraduates get above 5 LPA at all — so these numbers are at or slightly above market for the location and sector, not a lowball. Good fit for someone who wants solar/transmission manufacturing domain depth in Rajasthan and can accept a compressed cash band; poor fit for anyone optimising for first-job comp or for a structured graduate programme.

estimated_roles.why: Ringg is already hiring Forward Deployed Engineers with this round — that role exists because enterprise voice agents do not self-serve: someone has to sit with a Practo or a Policybazaar, map the call flow, configure the agent, run the pilot and hold the account through go-live. The business-side half of that work (onboarding, QBRs, expansion, escalation triage) is a standard entry seat that a 40-55 person company splits off from the FDE function as soon as account count outruns engineer time. Handling ~20M call attempts a month across named enterprise logos makes that inevitable within 6-12 months. Strong fit for an engineering grad who wants a customer-facing career without being an SDR.

estimated_roles.title: AI Conversation Designer / Voice Agent Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Product analyst and associate product manager
estimated_roles.why: The round funds proprietary in-house speech models and the 'context graph', and expansion into WhatsApp, chat and browser agents. Every one of those surfaces needs someone writing and tuning prompts, designing call flows and intent trees, and grading transcripts to find where the agent broke — the voice-AI-native version of an entry product-analyst seat. This is a role category that barely existed two years ago and is now standard at every serious voice-AI company, and it is one of the few business-track jobs where a fresh engineering graduate can outperform an experienced non-technical hire from day one. Not posted today, but at 20M monthly call attempts the volume of transcript-QA and flow-tuning work already exceeds what the founders and FDEs can absorb.

estimated_roles.title: Business Analyst - Founder's Office / GTM Strategy
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Classic post-raise hire at an Indian Series A: fresh capital, a board with Peak XV and Arkam on it, and three new geographies (Middle East, US, GCC accounts) to size and sequence. Someone junior has to build the pricing model, the cost-per-minute unit economics (which matter enormously here — the round is partly about building internal GPU infrastructure to cut inference cost, and that thesis needs a spreadsheet owner), the investor reporting pack and the market-entry research. Marked 'possible' rather than 'likely' because at 40-55 people the founders often still do this themselves, and when they do hire, they frequently take an ex-consulting or IIM candidate over a fresh engineering graduate.

estimated_roles.title: Growth Marketing Associate (Demand Generation)
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing
estimated_roles.why: The company currently has one marketing opening and it is an intern, which tells you the function is thin — one or two people covering content, demand gen, events and product marketing for a company entering three new geographies and three new product surfaces. Post-raise, funded B2B startups reliably add a junior demand-gen seat to feed the SDR pipeline: paid search on high-intent voice-AI keywords, LinkedIn ABM against enterprise accounts, webinars, and the conference circuit in the Middle East and US. Possible rather than likely because it may simply be the content intern converting and absorbing the scope instead of a separate hire.

estimated_roles.title: Voice Operations & Call Quality Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: Roughly 20 million call attempts a month is an operations problem before it is an AI problem: connect rates, carrier and telephony routing, DLT/TRAI compliance for outbound Indian calling, do-not-disturb scrubbing, per-campaign answer and drop rates, and sampled QA of what the agent actually said on a KYC or loan-collections call. Someone junior owns that dashboard and escalates the failure patterns to engineering. Regulated use cases (KYC, collections) make the compliance-QA half non-optional. Priced at the lower-middle of its benchmark row, not the analyst half — see band_basis.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and worth being precise about why. On the positive side: this is a genuinely fresher-friendly *kind* of company — B2B voice AI, one Bengaluru office, well funded ($15.5M), growing fast (15+ hires in three months on a ~40-person base), and the round explicitly funds GTM/enterprise-sales expansion in India, the Middle East and the US, which is exactly the budget line entry-level business hires get paid from. An engineering graduate is also unusually well matched to the non-engineering seats here: conversation design, prompt/call-flow QA and enterprise deployment for voice agents all reward someone who can read a transcript log, reason about failure modes and talk to an API, which is a fresher CS/ECE grad's actual skill set, not an MBA's. Against: today there is exactly one door a 0-1 yr candidate can walk through — the Technical Content Writer Intern role. Of the five live openings, one is engineering (Forward Deployed Engineer, excluded), the Technical Product Manager and Visual & Motion Designer roles want real experience and a portfolio/track record, and the SDR posting asks 2-3 years. At 40-55 people there is no management-trainee scheme, no APM programme, no campus process and no HR machinery to run one — hiring is ad hoc and referral-led, so the realistic fresher path is intern-to-full-time conversion or a cold approach for an SDR/CS seat that gets created rather than posted. Not "poor" — the roles are real, the money is there and the work suits the profile — but not "good" either, because there is no structured fresher intake and the posted bar sits above 0-1 years across the board.
companies.caveat: Every number here is an estimate derived from benchmark rows plus judgement. Ringg AI has published no salary band, and no source I used reports a single actual Ringg offer — the bands come from AmbitionBox/Glassdoor/Levels.fyi India market rates for Series A-B Bengaluru startups, adjusted for this company's size. Four of the seven roles below do not exist yet: only the SDR and the content-writer internship are actually posted, and both ask for experience the target candidate does not have. Also flag the source row itself: data/todo_part1.json index 10 records "Series A, 96.3Cr, 2026-07-22, Peak XV Partners[+3]", but press (TechCrunch, Entrackr, YourStory) reported this as a ~$10M Series A EXTENSION announced 25 August 2026, on top of a $5.5M Series A in January 2026 led by Arkam — the DB date/amount look like the ROC filing/allotment, not the announcement. That does not change the band (extension or not, it prices as Series A-B), but it means "Series A" here is a bigger, later company than a fresh Series A. Legal entity is Stoic AI Private Limited (CIN U62090KA2023PTC180343), formerly the TTS product DesiVocal — a registry search on "Ringg AI" alone finds nothing. Headcount (~40, TechCrunch, late Aug 2026, 15+ hired in the prior quarter) is two weeks old on a fast-hiring company: treat it as a floor, and note that if headcount doubles in 12 months the hiring bar loosens and structured fresher intake becomes plausible where today it is not.

companies.fit_reason:
Mixed, and closer to poor than the funding headline suggests. What works: an eight-year-old manufacturer that just raised Rs 230Cr to expand a plant and commercialise four newer ingredient lines genuinely needs junior commercial and supply-chain hands, headcount is climbing fast (Tracxn recorded 39 in Aug 2025 against ~79 LinkedIn profiles now), and tier-2 manufacturers are more willing than metro startups to take an untested graduate into an executive-grade seat.

What works against it, and a 2026/2027 graduate should weigh this honestly. (1) Most of the hiring this round funds will be technical, not business — plant operators, production and QA/QC chemists, microbiologists, R&D associates, food technologists. Those are real fresher openings, but they want B.Tech Food Tech, Biotech, Chemical or an M.Sc, and they are engineering roles, not the business track this question asks about. A CS/IT/mechanical graduate looking for a business seat is competing for a much smaller set. (2) There is no careers page at all — arborealbio.com has no jobs route — so there is no campus programme, no structured management-trainee intake and no fresher pipeline to apply into. Everything runs through LinkedIn and Naukri, one requisition at a time. (3) The single opening I could verify today, Senior Executive - EXIM, is an experienced hire with 200+ applicants; a fresher does not clear it. (4) Business-track pay here is low in absolute terms — Rs 3-5L fixed for most of these seats — because it is a Lucknow manufacturer, not a Bengaluru startup, and the "Series A" label creates an expectation the pay will not meet. (5) Location is a real filter: the plant and the commercial office are in Lucknow, and a graduate unwilling to be based in UP has only the thin, uncertain New Delhi option.

Net: worth applying to speculatively for supply-chain, EXIM and B2B sales seats, and an unusually good learning environment if you want ingredients/CPG manufacturing exposure early. Not a company to build a placement plan around, and not one that will come to campus.

companies.caveat:
These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not published bands — Arboreal has published no salary information, and only one of the five roles below is a confirmed live opening.

Specific limits on this estimate. The four predicted roles are inferred from what the round funds (plant capex, R&D, commercialising yeast protein, cocoa, collagen and fibres) and from an obvious B2B business need, not from any posting I could see. Because there is no careers page, the hiring picture is assembled entirely from third-party boards and is near-certainly incomplete — a company that just raised Rs 230Cr to expand a plant is recruiting plant, QA, supply-chain and sales staff off-platform, through referrals and local consultants. Two roles I found were deliberately excluded: "EA to Directors" (Lucknow) is confirmed expired, LinkedIn 301-redirects it with trk=expired_jd_redirect; "Distribution Manager" (Lucknow, Naukri) dates from July 2025 and is stale. The "Senior Marketing Manager - B2B" (Rs 10-30L) that motivated the Marketing Executive prediction sits only on an aggregator, getmereferred.com, dated 29 Jan 2026, and I could not corroborate it — aggregators routinely fail to expire listings, so treat it as unconfirmed and worth a direct check.

Every benchmark row I used is flagged "low" confidence by its own author and is explicitly extrapolated rather than measured — no source segments Series A-B employers by non-metro city, and the tier-2 numbers come from applying a published 15-30% discount to metro data. The manufacturer and true-tier-2 adjustments on top of that are my judgement, not sourced.

Two facts remain unresolved. The LinkedIn profile lists HQ as New Delhi while all funding coverage and the corporate registry say Lucknow; the plant is definitely in Lucknow, and a Delhi-based commercial or founder's-office seat would price 20-30% above these bands. And the "Series A" label is misleading for pricing — this is the first institutional round into an already-operating eight-year-old manufacturer, so the tech-startup Series A-B rows fit it only loosely in either direction. Finally, note the name collides with Arboreal Management (US), Arbor Biosciences and Arbor Biotechnologies; none of those are this company.

It is genuine fresher-accessible work: first-article and in-process dimensional inspection, CMM/gauge measurement, and AS9100/NADCAP paperwork on jet-engine and oilfield parts. Directly downstream of the round: capacity expansion across India, the UK and the USA plus the new Hardware Park campus means more parts inspected, and aerospace customers (GE, Pratt & Whitney, Safran, Collins) will not accept product without the inspection headcount behind it. Caution on the listing itself — it lives in a hardcoded JS bundle last touched 29 May 2026, so confirm it is live.

estimated_roles.title: Graduate Management Trainee - Operations / Supply Chain
estimated_roles.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programme
estimated_roles.why: The single most probable way a fresher actually enters this company on the business side. A 1,200-person group opening a new integrated campus and a 100-acre Andhra Pradesh site (1,000 projected direct jobs) staffs the middle of its org through a rotational trainee cadre — that is the standard Indian manufacturing pattern, and it is cheaper than lateral hiring at the pace this round demands. Expect a 12-18 month rotation across production, planning, stores, quality and sourcing before confirmation into one function. Not currently posted, and likely to surface through campus placement or Naukri rather than the website.

estimated_roles.title: Procurement / Sourcing Executive (Buyer - aerospace components)
estimated_roles.family: Operations and supply chain
estimated_roles.why: Supply Chain is a published 26-person function inside a group whose stated use of funds is capacity expansion across plants in three countries. Scaling machining output means scaling raw-material buys (titanium, Inconel, aluminium billet), special-process vendors (heat treat, NDT, plating) and inbound logistics across India, the UK and the USA — buyer seats grow roughly in step with output. Freshers enter here as junior buyers doing RFQ floats, PO release, vendor follow-up and expediting under a category manager. Reinforced by the fact that the portal already carries a Supply Chain Manager requisition: a manager hire is usually followed by executive-level headcount underneath.

estimated_roles.title: Production Planning and Control (PPC) Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations and supply chain
estimated_roles.why: With 10+ facilities and an order book above Rs 2,500 Cr, load-balancing work across machines and plants is the constraint that decides whether the new capacity actually converts to revenue. The Hardware Park campus build-out makes this sharper — someone has to sequence which part goes to which site during transition. Entry-level PPC work (releasing work orders, maintaining ERP routings, tracking WIP and on-time delivery) is a standard fresher landing spot for mechanical and production graduates and is a natural exit from the MT rotation.

estimated_roles.title: Quality Management Systems / Document Control Associate (AS9100, NADCAP)
estimated_roles.family: Operations and quality (compliance)
estimated_roles.why: Aerospace and defence work is certification-bound, and certification is administrative labour: control plans, FAIR/PPAP packs, non-conformance reports, corrective actions, calibration records, customer and registrar audit prep. Expanding to a new campus and adding own-IP product lines (micro turbojets, missile subsystems, UAVs) multiplies the documentation load and usually forces a fresh certification scope at the new site. QA is already a published 32-person function. This is one of the few genuinely non-engineering-heavy seats a manufacturer opens to freshers, and it teaches a compliance skill set that transfers across the whole aerospace supply base.

estimated_roles.title: Costing and Estimation Analyst (RFQ / build-to-print quoting)
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and finance-adjacent
estimated_roles.why: A build-to-print machining group lives or dies on quoting accuracy — cycle-time estimates, material yield, special-process cost, overhead absorption per machine hour. Two things in this round make the seat more likely: winning more work across three countries means quoting far more RFQs, and the stated move up the value chain from contract machining into own-IP propulsion and autonomy means someone must model cost structures for products that have no historical quote to copy. Manufacturers routinely hire mechanical/industrial freshers into estimation because the job needs shop-floor process intuition more than years of finance. Corporate-office seat, so it prices slightly above the plant-floor roles.

estimated_roles.title: Business Analyst - ERP / Digital Technology
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: Digital Technology is a published 18-person function, and a group running 10+ plants across India, the UK and the USA after two overseas acquisitions (PMC, WMT Precision) has an obvious systems-integration problem: consolidating ERP/MES, standardising master data, and building production and OTD reporting for investors who now sit on the cap table. Post-round institutional reporting discipline alone tends to create one or two analyst seats. A fresher here would do requirements gathering, UAT, report/dashboard building and data cleanup rather than architecture. Rated possible rather than likely because small manufacturers often outsource this to an implementation partner instead of hiring in-house.

estimated_roles.title: Associate - Strategy and Programme Management (CEO's Office)
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy
estimated_roles.why: The group is standing up a CEO's office around its new business lines — it has live requisitions for a CEO - Designate (Engine Division) and a Business Manager to the CEO, and the round explicitly funds the Mission Systems and Deep-Tech / Autonomous Systems units, which need programme tracking, investor reporting, partner and MoD/DRDO liaison support. The catch, and the reason this is only 'possible': the group's own analogous posting asks for 7-9 years plus B.Tech + MBA, so a fresher version of this seat is uncommon and would most likely come through a premium campus or a strong internal referral rather than an open posting. Highest-ceiling role on this list and the fastest exposure to leadership, but the least reliable to plan around.

companies.fit_reason:
Mixed, and the split runs along degree discipline rather than along ambition. In favour: this is a genuine volume fresher employer. It has 1,200+ people, is opening an integrated campus at Hardware Park, has flagged a Rs 500 Cr / 100-acre Andhra Pradesh expansion projected to create 1,000 direct jobs, and manufacturers of this size run standing GET/MT intakes because they cannot staff a growing multi-plant footprint any other way. A 2026/2027 mechanical, production, industrial or aeronautical B.Tech has a real, well-worn path in — and aerospace machining under AS9100/NADCAP is a rare, compounding skill base that transfers to GE, Safran, Collins and every Tier-1 in the country.

Against: the BUSINESS-track surface specifically is thin. The functional headcounts the company publishes are Engineering 124, Manufacturing 87, Operations 45, QA 32, Supply Chain 26, Digital Technology 18 — meaning the entire non-shop-floor population is a few hundred people, and the annual fresher intake into it is realistically a handful of seats, mostly filled through an MT/GET rotation rather than through a titled "Business Analyst" or "Growth Associate" requisition. Every opening with a verifiable July 2026 post date is senior: CEO - Designate (Engine Division), Business Manager to the CEO (7-9 years, B.Tech + MBA), Head - Manufacturing Automation. Even the careers-portal's Supply Chain Manager is a manager-grade seat, not a fresher one. So the honest read: strong fit for an engineering graduate willing to enter through operations, quality, planning, sourcing or costing and accept plant-floor pay; poor fit for a pure BBA/B.Com/marketing profile, and poor fit for anyone expecting product, growth-marketing, category or SaaS-style GTM work — those functions barely exist here. Two more things a candidate should price in: pay for these roles is roughly half what a Hyderabad GCC pays a fresher analyst, and most of these jobs are physically at Kurmalguda / IDA Gandhi Nagar / Hardware Park with shift exposure, not at a city-centre office. Also note defence and aerospace work carries customer/ITAR-adjacent security screening — Indian nationality and a clean background check are usually prerequisites.
companies.caveat: These are modelled estimates from third-party benchmark rows plus sector adjustments I made by hand. Raghu Vamsi has never published a salary band, and nothing here comes from an RVAG offer letter, a candidate report, or an AmbitionBox/Glassdoor page for this employer — there is effectively no employer-specific India pay data for this group at entry level. Three further limits: (1) the four careers-portal roles are hardcoded inside the site's JavaScript bundle (last modified 29 May 2026, two stamped REQ-2025-xx), so "Quality Assurance Inspector" may be seeded or stale content rather than a live requisition — verify before treating it as open; (2) the group actually recruits through LinkedIn and Naukri, and its three verifiable July 2026 openings never appeared on its own site, so assume unposted roles exist and ask; (3) these bands apply to the Indian entities only — PMC (UK) and WMT Precision (USA) pay on entirely different scales and should be modelled separately. Treat every number as a planning prior for a first conversation, not as a target to negotiate against.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and closer to poor than the careers page's twelve role cards make it look. Against the fresher: this is a 32-35 person wealth house whose two revenue-defining seats — Relationship Manager and Portfolio Manager — are senior hires by definition (a private-bank RM is hired for an existing HNI/UHNI client book, and Veriqus's whole thesis is recruiting veteran bankers and independent wealth creators who bring assets with them), so I deliberately did not price them for a 0-1 year graduate no matter that they head the careers list. Legal and Compliance, Risk Management and Finance are CS/LLB/CA-gated. There is no campus programme, no graduate scheme, no per-role posting, no level or location on any card, and applications go to a shared careers@veriqus.com inbox — this is a hiring-intent page, not a job board, and at this headcount each function may be one or two people. An engineering degree is also a mild negative on the investment side, where Mumbai entry hiring runs CA/MBA-finance/CFA and SEBI's Research Analyst qualification list does not include engineering. For the fresher: the round is founding capital for a build, and builds need juniors — the platform is explicitly AI-and-tech-at-its-core with portfolio analytics, risk monitoring and client reporting to specify, there is no separate software-engineering posting anywhere despite that framing (the tech org surfaces only as a Head of Information Technology), and a licence-acquisition plus book-migration phase generates real onboarding, KYC and ops volume. So the honest read: Product, Business Analyst - Wealth Platform, Ops and Tech, and the Internship are genuine doors for an engineering graduate; Service RM and the KYC/ops seats are attainable but pay near BFSI back-office rates; Investment Analyst and Research Analyst are attainable only with CFA L1/L2 or NISM plus modelling evidence; and the headline RM/PM roles are not fresher roles at all. Apply by email with the exact card title in the subject line, and expect to be assessed for the internship first.

companies.fit_reason:
Scimplify is hiring hard — 78 roles open at once — but almost none of it is aimed at graduates. Count the ladder: the live list is dominated by Business Head, General Manager, Manager, Senior Manager and Assistant Manager titles, plus a US business-development floor in eight American cities, and the company's own profile notes its senior commercial hires are experienced chemicals-industry people. Specialty chemicals is a domain-credential business: a customer buying a custom molecule wants a salesperson who can discuss synthesis routes and regulatory filings, which is not a 0-1 year hire. That is the case against.

The case for is real too, which is why this is mixed rather than poor. Three or four genuinely fresher-grade seats are live right now — Lead Generation Executive and its internship in Bangalore, Executive Operations in a brand-new vertical, Associate SCM (Purchase) at Attibele, Executive Lab Admin. More importantly, a company growing from Rs 17.7 Cr to Rs 200 Cr in one year and opening four new chemistry verticals plus a US go-to-market floor generates junior rungs mechanically: someone has to research the accounts, cut the POs, chase the customs broker and chase the vendor. An engineering graduate — especially chemical, mechanical or industrial — is a better fit here than at a pure software startup, because the technical vocabulary is an asset in the buying and coordination seats.

Two practical cautions. First, the pay is startup-scale in title but chemicals-scale in rupees: expect Rs 4-7L fixed in Bengaluru and Rs 3.5-5.5L in Lucknow or Gujarat, well below what the same "Series B startup, Bengaluru" label implies at a SaaS company. Second, the entry point is narrow — realistically the internship or the Lead Generation Executive seat, then internal movement. Applying to the Assistant Manager and Manager roles as a fresher will not work.
companies.caveat: Every number here is an estimate built from the benchmarks file, not a published band — Scimplify has disclosed no salary range for any role, and none of the sources behind those rows covers specialty chemicals specifically, so the sector adjustment in band_basis is my judgement rather than a measured figure. Confidence is set to LOW, one step down from the medium of the rows I leaned on, for three reasons the rules call out: the stage is genuinely ambiguous (the export labels the Rs 180.87 Cr Hitachi Ventures round a Series B while press coverage calls it a Series C, and the Rs 181 Cr may itself be a tranche of a larger $30-40M raise), the company sits awkwardly between the Series A-B and Series C+ rows, and headcount is unresolved — the careers page says "250+" while live job posts say "450+", and that same post boilerplate still cites the March 2025 Series B as the latest raise, so it is stale copy. Two further notes: seven of the thirteen roles are predictions, not postings, and are marked likely or possible accordingly — only the six marked "listed now" carry exact titles from the careers page, and those can be filled or pulled at any time. The two International Business internships on the page are New Jersey and Dubai seats, not India-priced, so I left them out. GOOD: Deployment, project management and pre-sales are genuine 0-1 year entry points at an industrial-vision company, and a B.Tech in mechanical, electronics, instrumentation or EEE is the preferred background rather than a handicap — you are commissioning cameras on a bottling line and arguing about false-reject rates with a quality head, which is engineering work wearing a customer-facing title. The company's own funding announcement says it is hiring for nearly all roles, and international expansion plus 170+ deployed lines create exactly this kind of volume hiring. POOR: enterprise closing, product management and strategy. Selling a capex-flavoured inspection system to Unilever, P&G, ITC and SKF is a multi-stakeholder plant-level sale that this company will staff with people who already have manufacturing-industry relationships; a fresher is not getting that seat. Product at ~90 people is one small team doing UI and algorithm-flow design, hiring at 2-4 years. HR and Finance & Admin are on the careers page but are not engineering-graduate paths — those go to HR-specialist and B.Com/CA profiles, so I have deliberately not priced them. Team QA is also listed but is software testing of DeepInspect, an engineering track rather than a business one, so it is excluded here too. companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. SwitchOn has published no salary band for any role, and nothing here comes from an offer letter or a job posting with a number on it. The five entries marked "listed now" therefore use the careers page's own team wording verbatim ("Team Sales", "Team Deployment") because the instruction is to use the exact title from the profile — read them as evidence of which functions are hiring, not as postings you can apply to by that name. Expect the actual requisition to read "Deployment Engineer", "Project Coordinator", "Business Development Executive" or similar. (2) CONFIDENCE IS MARKED DOWN ONE STEP TO LOW. The underlying benchmark rows are medium confidence at best, and I applied a 10-20% deep-tech-hardware discount away from the SaaS and consumer comparables those rows are built from — that adjustment is reasoned, not sourced. Treat each band as a centre of gravity with roughly Rs 1.5-2 LPA of spread either side, not a bracket. (3) THE ROUND LABEL IN THE EXPORT IS WRONG. It says Series A; Inc42, Entrackr, YourStory, ET and SwitchOn's own LinkedIn all say pre-Series B. Amount, date, founding year and investors all reconcile (Rs 77.3 Cr / ~$8M; IvyCap Ventures lead with SIG Tattva and Trifecta Capital), so the company match is confirmed and both labels fall inside the same benchmark row — but do not repeat "Series A" back to anyone. (4) NAME COLLISION. There is an unrelated SwitchON Foundation and a Kolkata NGO trading as "Switchon" whose admin and field jobs dominate Naukri results. This is the Bengaluru vision-AI company founded by Aniruddha Banerjee and Avra Banerjee, product brand DeepInspect. Verify the employer before applying.

companies.fit_reason: NeoGeo hires engineering graduates in volume, but into engineering seats: four of the six roles on its careers page are technical, including 'GIS Engineer (Ten People needed)', two full-stack developers and an Android developer. Every non-engineering requisition it has actually posted — on the site and on LinkedIn — is mid-senior: six GIS Project Managers, GIS Business Development Managers, Assistant Manager Business Development (Autodesk), Assistant Manager Sales (Government/B2G), Regional Sales Manager. There is no visible management-trainee scheme, no campus process, and no working ATS. So a 2026/27 B.Tech graduate who specifically wants a business-track seat gets in through side doors — the tender and bid desk, project coordination under the PMs, presales support on the new platform push, project MIS — rather than a named programme, and is paid on engineering-services scale (3.5-6 LPA for the field-facing seats), materially below both NeoGeo's own GIS and software engineering seats and a Gurugram SaaS comparable. Mixed rather than poor because the roles genuinely exist and the round explicitly funds hiring against a live pipeline; mixed rather than good because the demand is unstructured, thinly paid, and the graduate's better-paid door at this same employer is the technical one. Note also that the posted 'GIS Project Managers (6 Managers needed)' role is deliberately excluded from the priced list above: it is a 4-8 year hire and pricing it as a fresher band would be misleading, even though it is the loudest signal on the page about where delivery-side headcount is going.

Confidence was lowered one step from the source rows' medium to low for two specific reasons: the stage is genuinely ambiguous (a Series A label on a revenue-generating mid-market SI, which moves the right answer by 40%+ depending on which read you take), and the hiring signal is stale — every requisition ID on the careers page reads 'NGI 2211-0xx', i.e. November 2022, and the linked ATS at cats.neogeoinfo.in is broken today (TLS name mismatch, HTTP 500 over https, 404 over http). LinkedIn is the live channel; the website is not. Six of the seven roles above are inferred from what the round funds and what a government SI structurally needs, not observed postings. Finally, the export's own record for this round is unreliable: it dates the round 2026-07-15 against a public announcement of 2026-08-18, its Rs 193 Cr against the reported $20M implies ~96.5 INR/USD so the true figure is probably nearer Rs 175-180 Cr, and it lists only 'Aavishkaar Capital[+1]', omitting co-lead Neev Fund II (SBI Ventures) — the omission that most changes the read, since DFI and PSU-bank-adjacent growth capital into a government contractor is what justifies pricing this on a services scale rather than a startup scale.

companies.caveat: The honest risk is not that the band is wrong — it is that the roles may not exist. Pixxel's live board is 19 of 25 spacecraft and space-systems engineering reqs, and there is not one growth, sales, marketing, business development, strategy, partnerships or founder's-office opening anywhere on it. Every business-side role currently posted (Business Finance Gov Contracts, Associate Director Finance US, SAP S4 Hana, Talent Acquisition Specialist, Image Product Manager) asks for 3-8 years, which means Pixxel's revealed preference for business functions is experienced laterals, not graduates. So there is a real chance that over the next 12 months this company opens zero true entry-level business-track seats in Bengaluru, and the only door for a 2026/27 grad stays the "Role Explorer" catch-all. Second risk: the band is derived entirely from consumer-internet and SaaS benchmarks because no Indian spacetech comparable (Pixxel, Skyroot, Agnikul, Dhruva) has enough self-reported entry-level business salaries to benchmark against — deep-tech pay can sit either below these rows (smaller commercial teams, mission-driven discount) or above them for anything image-science-adjacent. Third: for a 2026/27 engineering graduate specifically, Pixxel is far more likely to hire you into an engineering seat than a business one, and those pay on a different, generally higher scale — applying business-side is arguably fighting the company's actual demand. Fourth, a method caveat carried from the research: the job board sits in a Darwinbox iframe behind Cloudflare, so the openings list is a point-in-time read from 2026-09-10 and post-round reqs may already have changed it.

companies.fit_reason:
Mixed, and the mix matters more than the average. On the positive side, this is a genuine consumer-tech company in HSR Layout with real revenue (~100k paying users), operator founders from Meesho and Pocket FM, a Lightspeed-led round two-and-a-half months old, and money explicitly allocated to user acquisition and product — the exact conditions under which growth and analytics associates get hired. The positive side: this is a real, scaled consumer business with ~280-300 people selling across Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit and Zepto, and the functions it runs on — marketplace category management, listings and cataloguing operations, performance marketing, demand planning — are exactly the functions Indian D2C companies do staff with 0-1 year graduates, because the work is high-volume and learnable on the job. Third, the pay is genuinely modest — a budget-brand, loss-making P&L pays category and ops freshers ₹4-8 LPA, materially below the SaaS and consumer-tech offers a 2026/2027 engineering graduate in Gurugram will see alongside it. Not "poor", because the role types clearly exist and the business obviously needs them; not "good", because the company is not publishing openings, shows no graduate pipeline, and pays below the tech alternatives competing for the same candidate.

companies.fit_reason: Real entry-level business seats exist and the sector genuinely takes generalist graduates — EPR compliance ops, collection-network coordination and ESG/traceability reporting are all learnable from a B.Tech base, and a Rs 56 Cr infrastructure build closed in June will need staffing on the ground. (1) The hiring surface is nearly invisible: one non-engineering role displayed, no ATS, no jobs board, applications by email to careers@karosambhav.com on a site that self-labels beta, and the listings carry no date — so a fresher cannot tell what is live and has no funnel to apply into. The honest read: worth applying if the mission and the critical-minerals angle matter to you, and best entered through the ESG/traceability analyst or compliance route; a poor choice if you are optimising for first-job compensation.

companies.fit_reason: Entry is genuinely open but narrow, and it is not a tech entry. Of ~1,500-2,000 employees, the overwhelming majority are clinic-based — 175+ veterinarians plus clinic support staff — for whom the qualification is a BVSc, not an engineering degree; the Gurugram corporate HQ that actually hires graduates is likely only low hundreds of people. Of the nine openings visible today, four are clinical (Veterinarian x2, Veterinary Surgeon x2) and closed to an engineering graduate outright, two are craft roles that want portfolios and 2+ years (Content Manager, Packaging Designer), and three are realistically open to a 0-1 yr graduate: Inside Sales Specialist, Business Development Specialist and Performance Marketing. So there is a live door — but it opens onto consumer sales and marketing at services-sector pay (roughly 3.5-9 LPA fixed), not onto product or engineering. Vetic had no engineering roles posted at all on the day this was checked, and its older Program Manager / Product Manager listings have expired, so an engineering graduate joining here should expect to be doing business work, not to be converting into a tech track. The upside: a post-raise chain doubling its clinic count across 11+ cities and launching Vet-at-Home nationally within two quarters gives a junior person unusually early ownership of a real P&L or a city, which is worth more than the first-year number. Rated mixed rather than good because the pay ceiling is low and the tech path is absent; not poor, because there are live, fresher-appropriate, non-credentialed openings today.
companies.caveat: These are estimates derived from benchmark rows. Vetic has not published a salary band for any role, and nothing here comes from an actual Vetic offer. Four specific weaknesses to hold in mind. (1) The role list is not from the careers page: vetic.in/careers is a marketing page with a single Google Form and no individual listings, so the nine "currently open" titles were taken from Vetic's LinkedIn company postings (3-10 Sept 2026), cross-checked against a Glassdoor count of 9; only one, Inside Sales Specialist, was individually opened to confirm it is live. Treat the other "listed now" titles as high-probability rather than verified, and apply through the Google Form as well as LinkedIn. (2) The round letter is unreliable — the export says "Series D", the press says only "$40M led by Bessemer", other trackers say B or C. I priced on capital raised (~$45M total) rather than the letter, which is why bands sit on the Series A-B rows; if Vetic is genuinely later-stage than that, every band here is 20-35% low. This ambiguity is the main reason confidence is low rather than medium. (3) The benchmark rows themselves are built from SaaS, quick-commerce and consumer-tech salary data; no row in the file covers veterinary or clinic-chain services, so the sector discount I applied is my judgement, not an observed Vetic-sector figure.
