But the fit is mixed, not good, for three reasons. First, pay: these are hospitality-, sales- and site-shaped roles that land at ₹3-6.5L, roughly half what the same graduate would see from a Series C+ tech company in the same city, and the benchmark rows will flatter these offers badly if compared naively. Second, the work: an engineering degree buys you nothing in a community or leasing seat; the only genuinely degree-relevant track is fit-out/project coordination on the design-and-build side, which favours civil, mechanical and electrical grads over CS. Third, the front door: exactly one role is published today and it needs 5+ years, so there is no fresher pipeline to apply into. A company this size hiring off a one-role board is running requisitions privately — the realistic route is a direct approach to hr@incuspaze.com naming a specific centre or the Hyderabad expansion, not the careers page. Worth pursuing if you want operations or commercial real estate as a career; not worth it as a default first job for a CS/IT graduate with software options.

Two further Zoho records exist — "Captain" and "Hiring Request In Presales", both Udyog Vihar Sector 18 — but both carry Publish=false and are not open today; ask about them directly. (2) The source row in the export is wrong on two counts: ₹45.1 Cr on 2026-05-25 is a single RoC allotment tranche, and the real headline is ₹150 Cr announced 28-29 June 2026 led by Bharat Value Fund; and "Series A" is wrong for a company whose maiden round was July 2024. (3) band_confidence is low: the underlying benchmark rows are medium, and I stepped down one because the stage is genuinely ambiguous (the row choice between Series A-B and Series C+ is my judgment, and it moves the HQ bands by ₹2-4L) and because the sector haircut applied to every role is unsourced judgment — not one benchmark source covers a real-estate or coworking operator. Against it: all four currently listed roles are mid-level (three managers/experts plus a scientist seat), there is no ATS, no per-role posting, no campus process and no graduate programme — applications go to a single mailbox against a static list of titles on the homepage. Degree matters more than usual here: a B.Tech Biotech, Food Technology, Chemical or Industrial Biotech graduate is genuinely employable into the regulatory and procurement seats and can also carry a technical BD conversation; a CS/IT/mechanical/electrical graduate with no life-sciences background has close to nothing to apply for on the business side, and for that candidate the honest answer is poor. companies.fit_reason: This is a two-to-ten-person, one-year-old company that has raised its first institutional cheque and is spending it on platform build-out and market entry, not on headcount. There is no careers page (verified: /careers and /jobs both 404, the sitemap lists no jobs page, and the LinkedIn jobs tab is empty), so there is currently zero graduate hiring surface to apply through. The work itself is also unusually badly matched to a 0-1 year engineering graduate on the business side: the commercial job is selling programmatic trading and dispatch into North American and European wholesale power markets, where credibility comes from ISO market experience, and the technical job is forecasting and optimisation, which will go to quant and infra engineers. At this headcount the founders do the selling themselves. The one genuine opening is the founder's-office archetype — a strong premium-campus grad hired as generalist leverage for a founder — and that is a single seat, filled through investor and campus networks rather than an application form; Entrepreneurs First backing makes a network hire even more likely than a posted one. Two further practical warnings. First, the company's own website is a barely-customised template whose /about page still carries a vendor's fictional agency ("Vence", New York, invented staff) — that is not a fraud signal, but it does mean there is no reliable first-party source on team, office or leadership, so any candidate should insist on meeting the actual founders and seeing the Indian entity before accepting. Second, if the real employing entity is the Delaware company with a US-remote team, an India-based fresher may be offered a contractor arrangement rather than employment, with no PF, no gratuity and no Indian statutory protection. Advice: do not build a job search around this company. Treat it as a warm-intro target only, approached through the investors or an energy-markets community, and only if the specific pull is domain learning in power trading rather than pay or stability.

Rated mixed rather than good: the roles exist and the company is growing fast off a small base, but the pay, the route in and the degree relevance are all weak. Rated mixed rather than poor because a young NBFC scaling disbursals genuinely does absorb graduates, unlike a two-person seed company.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and honestly closer to the weaker end. The positives: this is a genuinely operations-hungry business - 5,000+ technicians, 90+ cities, 100+ brand contracts with SLAs - and companies of that shape do hire graduates in volume into coordination, dispatch and CX seats, so entry-level doors exist and a fresh engineering graduate can walk through them. The negatives are substantial. First, there is nothing publicly listed: wiffy.ai/career returns HTTP 200 but is an empty placeholder reading "We are still making this feature", and /join-us and /onboarding are technician recruitment, not corporate hiring - so a graduate has no application route today beyond a cold email. Second, the white-collar team is small (~200-250 people show Wiffy as employer on LinkedIn; the 1,001-5,000 LinkedIn band includes on-roll technicians), which means the corporate org opens single seats, not campus batches. Third, the work an engineering graduate would actually be hired into here is field-services coordination, not product or analytics - the pay is materially below what the same graduate would get at a SaaS or consumer-tech Series A, and the skills are less portable. The one role worth targeting deliberately is the Business/MIS Analyst seat, which sits closest to the AI workforce-management platform the round funds and is the only entry point with a clear technical progression.
companies.caveat: Every band here is an estimate derived from benchmark rows. Wiffy has published no salary band, and none of these six roles is currently listed - all are predicted, so likelihood is "likely" or "possible" and nothing is marked "listed now". Specific limits on this estimate: (1) The careers page is a live but empty placeholder, so I could not anchor any prediction to a real job description; the only corporate posting I found anywhere is a LinkedIn company post for "Accounts / Sr. Accounts Executive" (Andheri West, 1-3 yrs, apply to rajiv.jethva@wiffy.ai), which is roughly 6-7 months old, cannot be confirmed open, and is not a 0-1 year role anyway - so I did not include it. (2) Naukri, Indeed, Glassdoor and Jooble all blocked automated access, and web-search quota was exhausted during the underlying research, so open listings may exist that neither I nor the profile could see. (3) Band confidence is lowered one step from the medium-confidence benchmark rows because the white-collar org is small (~200-250), no openings are verifiable, and I applied a non-SaaS field-services discount that the benchmark rows themselves were not constructed to support. (4) The benchmark rows for BD, category and product-adjacent families are built largely from SaaS, e-commerce and quick-commerce comparables; a technician-network services company is a materially different pay market and I adjusted down for that throughout - if anything these bands may still read slightly high for the field-facing roles. (5) The DB's Rs 29.1 Cr against a reported $3M implies ~Rs 97/USD, so treat the rupee round size as approximate. Name collision warning: this is the installation-services firm (ex-WIFY, wiffy.ai), not wiffy.me the router product.

companies.fit_reason: There is a genuine door here, but it is narrow and it does not pay like a software Series A. Positives: 10 live postings at a ~100-person company is real hiring; Applications and Pre-Sales Engineer, Procurement Associate and Logistics Executive are all plausibly open to a 2026/27 engineering graduate, and the pre-sales seat is an unusually good first job for someone who wants a commercial career but has a mechanical/electronics degree. Negatives, and they are the bigger half: this is a manufacturer, so the centre of gravity is engineering and shop floor — 5 of the 10 open roles are engineering and two of the five non-engineering ones (Project Manager - Robotics, Finance Manager) are mid-career seats a fresher cannot touch. There is no management-trainee or graduate programme, no APM or product-analyst track, and no analytics function to hire into, so the "management trainee / graduate leadership" and "product analyst / APM" benchmark families simply have no seat at this company — I did not invent one. Business-role volume at this headcount is a handful of hires a year, hiring is likely to stay founder-led and ad hoc, and the ops titles that do take freshers sit in the ₹3-6.5L band, below what the same graduate would get at a Bengaluru SaaS Series A. Best-fit candidate: a mechanical, mechatronics, electronics or industrial-engineering graduate who wants factory-floor and customer-site exposure and is willing to trade first-year cash for it.
companies.caveat: Estimates only — ANSCER has published no salary band, and none of these numbers came from the company. They are benchmark rows adjusted by judgement, and individual offers at a founder-run 100-person startup vary more than any band implies. (2) Only three of these seven roles exist today; the other four are inferences from the stated use of funds (US operations, partner network, product platform) and the company may fill none of them, or may fill them with 2-4 year hires instead of graduates. (3) Applications and Pre-Sales Engineer (Robotics) is a judgement call as a "business-track" role — it carries Engineer in the title and will filter on an engineering degree, so if you want a strict non-engineering list, drop it. (4) Headcount (~80-120) is a LinkedIn-derived estimate with no company-published figure, and it feeds the "small company" discount and the one-step confidence downgrade to low: the underlying benchmark rows are medium confidence at best for these families, and the hardware/manufacturing adjustment I layered on top is not something the rows themselves measure.

companies.fit_reason: Scapia is the right kind of employer for a fresher on paper — a well-funded Bengaluru consumer fintech at genuine venture pay scale, with a round explicitly earmarked for hiring across product, data science, design and engineering — but the live board says the opposite about seniority. Every business-track role currently open is a senior one: Lead Product Designer, Senior Graphic Designer, Senior Visual Designer, Group Product Manager, Product Lead, Senior Product Manager. At ~250 people, a company scaling a regulated card programme buys domain experience rather than training it, and there is no graduate scheme, no APM programme, no management-trainee track and no campus-hiring signal anywhere in the profile. So a 2026/2027 engineering graduate is not shut out — analytics, growth/CRM and category-support seats are the realistic doors, and the round's customer-scaling and third-bank-partner workstreams create exactly that kind of headcount — but they will be competing against 2-4 year laterals for roles that appear irregularly, and the single most reliable entry route at a company of this shape is an internship that converts. Not "good", because nothing fresher-shaped is open today; not "poor", because unlike an NBFC branch network or a manufacturer, this business genuinely runs on analysts, growth operators and product people in a tier-1 city.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not published bands — Scapia has never disclosed a salary range for any role. Only one of the seven roles on their live board is even arguably fresher-accessible; the other five predicted roles are inferences from what the Series C round funds (scaling to millions of customers, a third bank partner, product expansion, an AI-first push) and from what a co-branded card business structurally needs, not from anything Scapia has posted. Two known data problems from the profile carry into this: "Category - Sell Side (Demand)" is listed exactly like that with no seniority marker, so its level is genuinely ambiguous and it may well be pitched at 2-5 years — if so, a fresher is not in scope for it at all and my Rs 6-12L band overstates what a 0-1 year candidate would see; and the contract "Product Support Engineer" sits under Engineering on their ATS even though the work is customer-facing, so treat my CX/disputes prediction as the shape of that hiring rather than a confirmed business-track opening. Job boards disagree on the count (Uplers 8, LinkedIn 15, company ATS 12), listings move weekly, and scapia.cards/careers returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so re-check https://scapia.freshteam.com/jobs before acting on any single title. companies.fit_reason: They clearly hire 0-1 year graduates at volume - a 95-centre chain running ~15 lakh patient visits a year cannot function without a steady intake of counsellors, front-office, centre-ops and claims staff, and the July 2026 acquisition batch plus the Rs 300-500 Cr expansion programme means more centres to staff. That is the "good" half. The "poor" half is threefold. First, pay: five of the seven roles land at Rs 2.6-5.0 LPA, below what the same graduate would clear in IT services or a GCC, and the well-paid rungs in the benchmark rows (SaaS BDR, big-tech BA, consumer-internet growth manager) simply do not exist in this organisation. Second, degree fit: hospitals staff counselling, centre ops and claims with BSc Optometry, BBA, B.Com and MHA graduates, so an engineering degree buys no edge and sometimes reads as a flight risk; the only two seats where it is a real advantage are the HQ MIS/analyst role and performance marketing, and both are single-digit-headcount teams in Dwarka. Third, access: the careers page carried only two senior clinical consultant vacancies when I checked it on 10 September 2026, and has no entry-level business posting at all, so a fresher has no advertised front door - realistically it is careers@centreforsight.net, Naukri, centre-level walk-ins and referrals. A graduate who wants healthcare-operations exposure and a fast path to running a centre P&L will find this a reasonable first job; one optimising for salary or for engineering-adjacent work should not treat this as a target.
companies.caveat: Every band here is an estimate built from the benchmark file plus stated adjustments. Centre for Sight has published no salary band, and none of these seven roles was advertised anywhere I could see. Four specific warnings. (1) NOTHING IS "LISTED NOW". I re-fetched the careers page on 10 September 2026: it shows exactly two vacancies, Senior Consultant - Cornea (Delhi, Safdarjung) and Consultant - Glaucoma Specialist (Mumbai, Andheri), both senior clinical posts requiring MS/DNB Ophthalmology plus a fellowship. Neither is entry-level, business-track, or open to an engineering graduate, so I deliberately did not carry them into likely_roles - listing them with a fresher band would have been false. All seven roles above are predictions. (2) THE FUNDING ROW DID NOT CONFIRM. The source entry's "Series B, Rs 90.2 Cr, 19 May 2026, Carillon Group [+4]" has no press or filings support, and "Carillon Group" appears in no reporting on this company. Do not repeat that framing to anyone as fact. The company's real, documented capital event is ChrysCapital's Rs 830 Cr / $100M in May 2024. The bands do not depend on the unconfirmed round - they are set by the company's size, sector and stage - but the round is why band_confidence is lowered a step. (3) BAND_CONFIDENCE IS LOW, FOR TWO REASONS: the unverified funding row above, and the fact that no benchmark row covers Indian healthcare-services delivery, so every number here required a judgement-call sector discount off rows anchored on consumer internet, big tech and SaaS. The underlying rows are medium-to-high confidence; my transfer of them to a hospital chain is not. Direction of error, if any, is more likely downward than upward - hospital non-clinical pay is compressed. (4) NAME COLLISION EXISTS. There is a UK Centre for Sight (East Grinstead, also founded 1996) and a Center for Sight in Florida. I priced the Indian chain, matched on rupee-crore denomination, the founded-1996 / 30-year anniversary the Indian chain marked in March 2026, and the all-Indian composition of the source file. If the intended entity is either overseas one, discard this row entirely.

companies.fit_reason: Real entry-level business roles exist at a company this size - supply chain, export documentation, MIS and field sales are all genuine fresher intakes in Gujarat manufacturing, and a new plant landing within six months plus a domestic and international scale-up mandate means hiring volume is rising. First, nothing at fresher level is posted: the official careers page carries no vacancies at all, only culture copy and a contact CTA, and every role traceable today is 2-20 years of experience (two Regional Sales Manager posts, a 2-5 year export coordinator, an accounts executive, a closed 18-20 year retail head). Second, the pay across the whole business track is 3-6.5 LPA, materially below what a 2026/2027 engineering graduate clears in IT services or a tier-2 GCC, with no equity to offset it. Third, an engineering degree is not the target credential for most of these seats - export documentation and accounts hire commerce graduates, farm sourcing hires agriculture graduates, and the genuinely engineering-shaped work here is plant and process engineering, a technical track outside this brief. Honest read: worth applying to for the MT or supply-chain path if you want manufacturing operations experience and are based in Gujarat, but do not treat it as a business-analyst or product-adjacent entry point, and do not expect a fresher-friendly funnel.

Two things stop this being a "good": there is no way in, and the pay for the seats they will actually open is low. On access: there is no careers page, no ATS tenant (Keka, Freshteam, Zoho, Greenhouse and Lever all come back empty), no careers/jobs subdomain, and the LinkedIn guest jobs API on their real company ID (f_C=96449689) returns zero postings against a control that returned ten. Hiring is founder-led through networks and recruiters, so a graduate with no referral has no application channel beyond a cold general inbox or a LinkedIn approach to Kunal Mundra or Nikhil Aggarwal. On pay and volume: at ~60-100 people the total business-side graduate intake is likely low single digits a year, there is no management-trainee or campus programme, and the two roles they most plausibly add in volume (fleet ops, lease ops) sit at ₹3.5-7L, below what the same graduate would get from a software company in Gurugram. The best-paying seats — founder's office, product, and anything in finance or credit risk — will go to experienced hires, which the profile itself flags: senior finance and risk hires here command near-market corporate comp precisely because the lending book makes those roles load-bearing. companies.caveat:
Estimates from benchmark rows, not published bands. Astranova has never published a salary figure and, as of today, has published no job at all — every role below is predicted from what the business obviously needs and what the round funds, not observed from a listing, so none can be marked "listed now" and all six titles are my wording rather than theirs.

Confidence is set to low, one step below the medium carried by most of the benchmark rows I used, for two reasons the rules call out. The company profile is verified=false: the identity is solid (the Inc42 report matches the database row on amount, date, founding year and all four investors, and this is definitively not AstroNova Inc / NASDAQ: ALOT), but nobody loaded a careers page or a real listing, because none exists. And the company is small — roughly 60-100 people — where a single founder's decision moves an offer more than any market band does.

Two further limits on the underlying research. Naukri, Indeed India, Foundit, Glassdoor, Instahyre, Wellfound and AmbitionBox all blocked the crawl with 403s, so a live posting could be sitting behind one of those walls — Naukri is the plausible one, since Indian fleet-ops companies do use it for field and service roles. And the recent rebrand from Electrifi Mobility left two stale LinkedIn pages (/company/astranova-mobility and /company/electrifi-mobility) alongside the live one (/company/astranovamobility, 62 employees); any headcount or hiring signal keyed to the wrong slug will badly understate this company, and the headcount estimate feeding my "tiny company" downgrade is itself approximate.

Finally, the bimodal risk in the ops band is real and worth restating: "Fleet Operations Executive" at this company could mean a ₹4L hub-supervisor seat or a ₹10L central-ops seat owning city P&L, and the same title is used for both across the Indian mobility sector. Read the job description, not the title.

companies.fit_reason: Nothing on the careers page today is open to a 2026/2027 graduate, and that is the honest headline. All 23 live roles are senior — most ask 8-15 years, several are "Head of"-level (Finance Controller, Contract Manager, Data Center Energy & Land Commercial Manager, Datacenter Power & Utilities Lead, Principal/Distinguished Solution Architect), and even Product Designer and the TA/employer-branding Recruiter read as mid-career at a 40-person company with no one to train a fresher. So none of these are marked "listed now": using an exact senior title as a fresher target would be misleading. What keeps this from "poor" is the shape of the company rather than the current board. Two of the three founders (ex-OYO global COO/CPO, ex-McKinsey partner) come from the exact backgrounds that hire founder's-office analysts off premium campuses, the round funds APAC expansion and a data-centre build-out that generates real coordination and analysis work, and 23 openings against ~40 people means the org is about to acquire the middle layer it currently lacks. Realistically that is one to three fresher business seats over the next 12-18 months, filled through referrals, a targeted campus or a cold approach — not a graduate programme. A fresher who gets in will be the most junior person in the room with no structured onboarding, which is high-learning and high-risk in equal measure. Engineering graduates who can code should note the other 16 roles are engineering (GPU orchestration, CUDA kernels, inference systems) — also senior, but a stronger long-run door into this company than the business track.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and the split runs straight down the middle of the company. The good half: KreditBee has a real Bengaluru product and analytics core, and it is hiring into it right now - Associate Product Manager (Lending), Associate Product Manager/Product Analyst, Business Analyst, Analyst/Senior Analyst - with Senior Data Analyst and Senior Data Scientist reqs open behind them. That is exactly where an engineering degree is an advantage, and the round's stated uses (AI for credit risk, platform strengthening, personalised products) fund those teams. The poor half, which is most of the company: of roughly 85 openings on the portal, the overwhelming majority are mid-to-senior field-sales, branch, credit and collections roles - City Head, Branch Manager, Cluster Head, Area Sales Manager, DSA Manager, National Collection Manager - that want 4-10 years of NBFC experience and will not consider a 2026 graduate. Two further frictions: KreditBee runs no visible campus or management-trainee programme, so there is no structured graduate door; and even the product and analytics reqs are written for 1-3 years, meaning a fresher is arguing their way in rather than applying to an open fresher slot. companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows and comparable-company data. KreditBee has published no salary band for any of these roles, and nothing here is sourced from the company. Specific limits to keep in mind. (1) Confidence is set to low, one step below the medium of the underlying benchmark rows, because the stage does not map cleanly onto a single row - a Series E pre-IPO NBFC straddles "Series C+" and "listed/large" - and because every row I used is built from SaaS, consumer-tech and quick-commerce comparables rather than from lenders, so the NBFC discount I applied is a judgment call, not a measured adjustment. (2) The listings are a snapshot of 2026-09-10 from a portal that turns over fast; the six "listed now" titles are reproduced exactly as posted (including the portal's own typography) and may already be closed. The Freshteam department labels are unreliable - several engineering roles are filed under Finance, Product and Risk & Data - so roles were classified by title. (3) The five predicted roles are inference from the round's stated uses of funds and from the manager-level reqs already open; none is confirmed to exist. (4) The round figure itself is imprecise: the export says Rs 2,040 Cr but the round was reported at $280M, of which roughly $220M is primary - the Rs 2,040 Cr almost certainly reflects only the primary slice. Founded year in the export (2017) is approximate; the underlying entities were incorporated in 2016. (5) Field, branch and collections bands are fixed cash only; realised earnings in those roles depend heavily on incentive attainment and can swing 30-50% either way.

Important caveat: at a 24-person seed company running semiconductor, defence and telecom deployments, this posting targets an experienced TPM (realistically 4-8 years), not a 2026/27 graduate. The band below prices the junior version they would more plausibly create later — a program/delivery associate sitting under the TPM, coordinating pilot deployments and customer documentation — not the posting as written. A 0-1 year grad applying to the live req should expect to be screened out.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office Associate (GTM & Enterprise Deployments)
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: GTM is still founder-led (zero sales, marketing, finance, HR or ops openings across 9 reqs). The seed funds scaling enterprise deployments and pushing into data centres, UAVs and robotics — that generates exactly the work a founder's office seat absorbs: RFP and security-questionnaire responses for defence/semiconductor buyers, on-prem/air-gapped deployment coordination, pipeline and investor reporting, compliance collateral for MISRA/AUTOSAR/ISO 26262/DO-178C claims. An engineering graduate is the right profile because the buyer is an embedded-systems engineering org. Most likely of the predicted roles to actually open in the next 12-18 months, though they will usually prefer 2-4 years over a fresher.

estimated_roles.title: Business Development Associate — Enterprise / Deeptech Accounts
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: Enterprise expansion is the stated use of funds and they already have live deployments to convert and replicate. A first junior BD/SDR seat — account research in automotive, aerospace, semiconductor and industrial-IoT, outbound to embedded-engineering and firmware leads, pilot coordination — is the standard first commercial hire after a seed. Pushed to 'possible' rather than 'likely': with a ~$2M round, long defence/semiconductor sales cycles and large technical ACVs, founders typically keep the selling themselves for another year or two rather than hand it to a fresher.

estimated_roles.title: Technical Content / Product Marketing Associate
estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing (technical content variant)
estimated_roles.why: Selling on-prem AI coding models to safety-critical engineering teams is won with technical credibility, not paid media: standards explainers (MISRA, AUTOSAR, ISO 26262, DO-178C), benchmark write-ups, deployment case studies, conference and developer-community presence. An engineering graduate who writes well fits this better than a marketing grad. Weakest of the three predictions — at 24 people this work usually sits with the founders or a research hire until Series A.

companies.fit_reason: This is a ~24-person seed deeptech with nine open reqs and zero of them in sales, marketing, finance, HR or operations. Eight of the nine are named technical roles; the ninth is an open talent-pool application. The single non-engineering posting, Technical Program Manager, is an experienced-hire role running defence and semiconductor deployment programs — not a graduate seat — and the two research roles are PhD-track. There is no structured graduate programme, no campus hiring signal, and GTM is still founder-led, which is entirely normal at this size and stage. A 2026/27 engineering graduate wanting to join H2LooP has a real path through the engineering ladder (Applied AI Engineer intern, AI Research Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer), but the business track here is close to non-existent today: the three predicted roles are things the company will plausibly need as it scales enterprise deployments into data centres, UAVs and robotics, and even when those open, a seed company with one small round usually buys 2-4 years of experience for its first commercial hire rather than training a fresher. The honest read is: watch this company for engineering roles, not business ones, and revisit the business track after a Series A.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not company data — H2LooP has published no salary band, and none of the live postings on their ATS (binary.so/h2loop) state compensation. Confidence is low: the underlying benchmark rows are medium-confidence at best and none of them tag employers by funding stage, and I lowered one step further because the company is tiny (~24 people on a single ~$2M round), where individual offers vary far more than any band and the founders' judgement on one hire moves the number more than the market does. Three of the four roles do not exist today and are inferred from what the round funds; they may never open, or may open only at 2-4 years of experience. Two data points on the company itself are unreliable: the tracker's founded year of 2024 conflicts with LinkedIn and Inc42, which both say 2025, and the ~24 headcount is LinkedIn-derived, not company-stated. Also do not confuse this company with the unrelated European "H2Loop" green-steel/hydrogen project.

A cross-functional seat reporting to the founder is exactly a founder's-office hire, and a 30-person pre-product company with Rs 100 Cr to deploy before a mid-2026 product reveal needs generalists who can hold four workstreams, not specialists.

estimated_roles.family: Growth and performance marketing (entry-level, 0-2 years, India) - brand/content variant
estimated_roles.why: OFF/BEAT is pitched at the intersection of AI, content and creators, and the founder is himself a media property. Brand and content is not a support function here, it is the product surface, and the pre-launch phase the round funds is almost entirely narrative-building: teaser, drop, community. boAt's playbook was brand-first, and this team is being built the same way.

A first product reveal expected mid-2026 means paid media, marketplace and D2C funnel work has to be staffed ahead of it. This is the standard first commercial hire a consumer seed makes after the brand lead.

estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management (entry-level, 0-2 years, India) - partnerships variant
estimated_roles.why: Every press description of the venture, however inconsistent, includes creators: 'content and creator-led platform', 'creator-economy monetisation'. Signing, onboarding and managing creators is relationship work that a 0-1 year hire can genuinely do, and it is the one function that has to exist before launch regardless of which product description turns out to be right.

estimated_roles.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM) - entry level, 0-2 years, India
estimated_roles.why: Product is one of the four areas the Gurgaon internships reportedly cover, and an AI-and-consumer venture will want someone on user research, funnel instrumentation and competitive teardowns once there is something to instrument. estimated_roles.title: Business Operations Associate (D2C / supply chain)
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

Contingent on the hardware read being correct, which is why it is possible rather than likely, and priced lowest of the six because ops and supply-chain entry pay in India sits well below the SaaS and product comparables the other rows lean on.

companies.fit_reason: The appetite is real, the access is not. On the positive side, this is one of the few seed companies where a 0-1 year business hire is the target rather than a compromise: reported average employee age is 24 excluding the founder, the visible hiring is Gen Z and intern-led in Gurgaon, the three surfaced internships work directly with Aman Gupta across marketing, operations, product and brand with a stated path to full-time, and there is a deliberate campaign inviting "failed founders" to apply. Business-track work is also the substance of the company, not overhead — a content, creator and consumer venture is mostly brand, growth and partnerships, so an engineering graduate crossing into business here is not competing against a large existing MBA bench. Against that: there are zero publicly listed roles today, no careers page, and no job-board presence anywhere I checked, so the only route in is a cold email to build@theoffbeatstudios.com or catching a founder post on LinkedIn/Instagram — a channel that rewards proximity and follower luck rather than a structured application. The team is about 30 people, so total entry-level seats are a handful, not a cohort, and inbound volume for anything attached to the boAt founder is extreme. Most importantly, the realistic first offer is a 3-6 month stipend internship that may or may not convert, not a full-time fixed CTC. A graduate with a fallback offer in hand can chase this; one without a fallback should not treat it as a placeable pipeline.
companies.careers_url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/theoffbeatstudios/ — no careers page exists; the LinkedIn About section reads "Building. For job opportunities: build@theoffbeatstudios.com". The official site https://www.theoffbeatstudios.com/ is a single Webflow teaser splash with no /careers, /jobs, /join or /hiring route and no sitemap, and the site listed on LinkedIn (offbeatkartakyahai.xyz) returns a Vercel 402.
companies.caveat: These are estimates built from benchmark rows, not published bands. OFF/BEAT has published no salary information, and neither has any company in this dataset. Three specific limits on the numbers above. First, none of these roles is confirmed open: the company profile is marked verified=false precisely because there is no careers page or live listing to read — LinkedIn's job API for the company returns an empty set, Unstop shows 0 jobs and 0 internships, and nothing appears on Internshala. Every title is inferred from what the round funds and what the business obviously needs, and the closest thing to evidence is a set of internships described in press coverage of the founder's social posts, which I could not open to quote exact titles from. Second, the role mix rests on an unsettled premise: published descriptions of what OFF/BEAT actually does contradict each other — "content and creator-led platform", "creator-economy monetisation infrastructure", "tech- and AI-led consumer venture", and one outlet calling it a venture studio that backs other founders. LinkedIn's Manufacturing classification is what pushed me toward the D2C-and-supply-chain reading, and if the venture-studio description turns out to be right, the operations and category-style roles largely disappear and the founder's-office and partnerships seats grow. Third, band_confidence is low rather than the medium most of the underlying rows carry, stepped down once for a company that is simultaneously tiny (~30 people), unverified, and pre-product — and all six bands are fixed cash excluding ESOP. Treat the fixed numbers as the range a full-time conversion offer would land in, and re-check the moment a first product reveal or an actual job posting appears.

estimated_roles.title: Project Associate - Farmer Onboarding and Field Operations
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: This is the single clearest read on the round. PTI/ET report the Rs 10 Cr is for accelerating on-ground operations and onboarding smallholder farmers, with a stated plan to take nature-based projects across 5 lakh hectares in 12-24 months. You cannot onboard farmers at that scale from a Gurugram office - it needs junior staff in the project districts registering farmers, running baseline surveys, coordinating soil sampling, chasing land records and consent paperwork, and reporting practice adoption (biochar application, AWD water regimes, agroforestry planting) back into the MRV system. It is the highest-volume, lowest-cost hire the round funds, and the Head of Operations they just posted for exists precisely to build a team like this beneath them. Reporting line would be that Head of Operations.

estimated_roles.title: Carbon Project Analyst (MRV and Registry Documentation)
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: The second funded workstream is strengthening the blockchain-powered digital MRV stack, and the third is commercialisation through offtake agreements - both of which generate a large, unglamorous documentation and data-QC load that sits below the CTO and above the field team. Someone has to reconcile field-collected practice data against remote-sensing outputs, prepare Verra/Gold Standard/Puro project design documents and monitoring reports, maintain the farmer and hectare registers, flag sampling gaps, and assemble the evidence packs that buyers and validators demand. This is the most engineering-graduate-friendly business role at Prithu: it rewards spreadsheet and light-Python fluency, GIS familiarity and methodology reading rather than agronomy credentials. Carbon registry documentation is also the classic entry-level seat at every peer (Varaha, Mitti Labs, Boomitra all staff it junior).

estimated_roles.title: Carbon Markets and Offtake Associate
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: The round explicitly funds expanding commercialisation through long-term offtake agreements with global buyers, plus international partnerships and new geographies - and against a 20 million tCO2e-by-2030 goal, someone has to build and work the buyer pipeline. At 17 people this sale is founder-led (Sunny Vaish will be in the room), so a fresher would not close anything; the realistic seat is buyer research, RFP and questionnaire responses, CDR-marketplace listings, pricing comparables, and drafting the diligence packs corporate buyers ask for. Marked possible rather than likely because a Rs 10 Cr round buys field capacity first, and a founder in a relationship-driven credit market often defers this hire until there is issued volume to sell.

estimated_roles.title: Founder's Office Associate
estimated_roles.family: Founder's office / chief of staff / strategy associate
estimated_roles.why: Three co-founders, a fresh institutional lead investor, a 24-month plan spanning 5 lakh hectares, new geographies and international partnerships, and no middle management - that combination reliably produces one generalist hire who does investor reporting, grant and accelerator applications, methodology and competitor research, unit-economics models per hectare, and whatever the week demands. Transition VC-backed companies commonly staff this seat post-round. Possible rather than likely because at 17 people the founders may simply absorb the work themselves for another year, and because when it is created it often goes to a tier-1 MBA or a repeat hire rather than a fresh engineering graduate. Note that if this role appears, it is the one most likely to be underpaid relative to its scope.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, and closer to poor than the headline "climate-tech raises funding" suggests. Against a fresher: the company is roughly 17 people with one Rs 10 Cr round, which is 2-4 business-side hires of any kind over the next year, not a cohort. There is no careers page, no graduate programme and no campus pipeline — hiring is ad-hoc LinkedIn posts. Both roles actually posted (Head of Operations, in-body "Senior Manager / Head - Operations", and Soil Scientist) are mid-senior and explicitly closed to a 0-1-year candidate: the ops role wants someone who can run field teams across states from day one, and Soil Scientist wants an M.Sc/PhD in soil science or agronomy. A B.Tech generalist matches neither. Prithu's field hiring will also lean toward B.Sc/M.Sc Agriculture graduates and people with FPO or extension-network experience over engineering graduates, because the work is agronomy and farmer trust, not systems. In favour of a fresher: the round is explicitly for boots on the ground — onboarding smallholder farmers toward a 5-lakh-hectare pipeline — and that kind of scale-up is exactly what gets staffed with cheap, mobile, junior project associates who will live in project districts. The MRV stack (remote sensing, ML, biogeochemical modelling, soil-sample calibration) also creates a genuinely engineering-flavoured business role — carbon project analyst — that a data-comfortable B.Tech grad can do better than an agri graduate, and that is the single best door in. Expect Rs 4-6L fixed, expect the work to be 60% field travel and registry paperwork, and expect to be one of two or three juniors with no manager layer above you. The learning is unusually good; the pay and the job security are not.
companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. Prithu has published no salary band, has no careers page at all (all hiring runs through LinkedIn posts), and has never posted a fresher role that I could observe — so every band here is a stage-and-family inference, not an observed offer. Two of the four benchmark rows I used are themselves marked "low" confidence and are triangulated from aggregators that do not tag employers by funding stage. Round data also drifts between sources (the tracker says 2026-04-07 / Rs 9.83 Cr; the PTI/ET story says Apr 29, 2026 / Rs 10 Cr — same round). The two live-ish listings are of uncertain status: fetched logged-out they render "No longer accepting applications", and a LinkedIn guest search for Prithu in Gurugram returns zero cards, so they may already be filled. Treat any number here as a starting point for a conversation, not a floor to reject an offer on.

estimated_roles.why: The whole product is affiliate and co-brand economics with Flipkart, Swiggy, Amazon, Myntra and Nykaa. companies.fit_reason: Right kind of employer, wrong moment in its hiring cycle. A Bengaluru consumer fintech with fresh capital and an explicit mandate to ramp hiring is exactly where business-track engineering graduates find work — and the growth, partnerships and product-analytics functions here are all genuine, fundable needs tied to the 1 Mn-user target. But of the seven posted business roles, six are Head, VP, Senior or Manager level; the company is buying a leadership layer it does not yet have, not graduates. Only the Business Intelligence Engineer posting is even arguably reachable at 0-1 years, and it is likely written for 1-3. At ~26 people there is no campus programme, no APM cohort, no structured onboarding, and hiring will be opportunistic — one seat at a time, filled by referral or a strong cold application to the founders, not a process. Realistic read for a 2026/2027 graduate: not "poor" (these roles will exist within 2-4 quarters and a fresher genuinely can do them), but you are applying into a company where you would be the most junior person by a margin and where the junior seats mostly have not been created yet.
companies.caveat: These are benchmark-derived estimates. GoSats has not published a salary band for any role, and none of the predicted junior titles above is currently posted — only "Business Intelligence Engineer" is live, and I have restated its exact title. Specific weaknesses to hold in mind: (1) The band confidence is one step below the benchmark rows' own "medium" because the company is tiny (~26 people) and the stage is ambiguous — a ₹46.5 Cr Series A on top of ~$5M raised in total behaves like a seed company, so the Series A-B rows arguably overprice it and the seed rows arguably underprice it; at this headcount an individual offer varies far more than any band. (2) The underlying research rests on a single outlet, Inc42's 07 Apr 2026 brief, with no second confirmation from Entrackr or Moneycontrol because web search was unavailable that session; Konvoy is normally a gaming/esports VC, which makes the pairing unusual even though the reporting is explicit. (3) The two unresolved "[+2]" investors and a founding year that differs across sources (2019 export / 2020 Inc42 / 2021 YC) mean the company's true age and backing are not fully pinned down. (4) Headcount is LinkedIn's self-reported count, which usually undercounts ops and non-technical staff, so the company may be somewhat larger than 26 — that would push bands up, not down. (5) The business is bitcoin-linked: both the hiring ramp and the value of any equity component are exposed to an asset price no benchmark row accounts for.

Growth-stage D2C brands hire 0-1 year executives into this function routinely because the work is measurable from day one.

estimated_roles.family: Category management and merchandising
estimated_roles.why: The business is a multi-category bag portfolio - hard-shell trolleys, laptop and school backpacks, duffels, accessories - and 'category growth' is exactly what the Rs 20 Cr is described as funding. A junior category seat owns SKU-level sell-through, pricing, assortment planning and new-launch coordination with the design and sourcing teams.

estimated_roles.title: E-commerce / Marketplace Operations Executive
estimated_roles.family: Operations and e-commerce channel management
estimated_roles.why: Marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra) are a stated channel, and someone junior has to own listing hygiene, A+ content, buy-box and pricing, ad campaigns inside the marketplace consoles, returns reconciliation and inventory sync. This is the highest-volume fresher intake in Indian D2C and the one an engineering graduate can do immediately.

estimated_roles.title: Supply Chain / Inventory Planning Associate
estimated_roles.family: Operations, supply chain and city launch
estimated_roles.why: A physical-goods brand with GRS-certified recycled-plastic hard shells runs on vendor lead times, import and production planning, warehouse stock cover and returns. Expanding retail and categories on Rs 20 Cr without more working capital makes demand forecasting and inventory turns the constraint, so a junior planner earns their seat.

estimated_roles.title: Business / Growth Analyst
estimated_roles.family: Business analyst and data analyst
estimated_roles.why: Flat valuation plus widening losses means the board conversation is unit economics: contribution margin by SKU and channel, blended CAC, returns rate, marketplace commission leakage. A single junior analyst supporting the founders and category leads is the cheapest way to get that, and it is the best-fit seat here for an engineering graduate. Least certain of the four operational roles because a ~100-person company may hand this work to the category and finance teams instead.

estimated_roles.title: Institutional / Corporate Sales Executive
estimated_roles.family: Business development, inside sales and account management
estimated_roles.why: The profile confirms institutional and corporate tie-ups are a real channel (Akasa Air) and that the company was hiring an Institutional Sales Manager - West in Mumbai about four months ago, that posting now expired. A manager hire in a function normally pulls a junior executive behind it for lead generation, corporate-gifting outreach and order coordination. Priced near the seed row and quoted fixed-only: this is a target-carrying field seat, not a SaaS SDR.

estimated_roles.title: Retail Expansion / Retail Operations Executive
estimated_roles.family: Retail operations and channel expansion
estimated_roles.why: Retail stores are a named channel and offline rollout is the most common use of an expansion top-up for a bag brand competing with VIP and Safari on shelf presence. The junior version of this is store-launch coordination, shop-in-shop and distributor support, visual merchandising checks and secondary-sales tracking - travel-heavy field work. Priced below the Series A-B operations floor because Indian retail and field roles pay far under the startup comparables the benchmark row is built from.

companies.fit_reason: Mixed, leaning difficult-to-enter rather than badly-paid. In favour: a D2C consumer brand selling through its own site, marketplaces, retail stores and institutional tie-ups genuinely runs the four functions that absorb freshers — performance marketing, marketplace/e-commerce ops, category/merchandising and supply-chain planning — and an engineering graduate's spreadsheet, SQL and ad-platform literacy is a real edge in the marketplace-analytics and growth-analyst seats, where most applicants are commerce or MBA candidates. The Rs 20 Cr is explicitly for "expansion and growth", which in this business means more SKUs, more offline doors and more institutional accounts, all of which need junior execution. Against it, and this is the bigger half: there is no careers page and zero live postings anywhere reachable, so there is no application flow at all — entry is only via LinkedIn outreach to the founders or HR, which most freshers will not do. The team is ~90-120 people with no structured management-trainee or graduate programme, so hiring is one-off and manager-driven. The founding team came out of VIP Industries and Samsonite, and that lineage tends to hire experienced category and channel-sales people rather than train graduates. And the money is a flat internal bridge into a business losing Rs 35 Cr on Rs 83 Cr of revenue, so headcount is likely being added narrowly, not broadly. Finally, the honest pay comparison: Rs 4-8L fixed is well below what the same 2026/2027 engineering graduate would clear in a software role, so this only makes sense as a deliberate move into consumer brand building.
companies.caveat: Every band here is an estimate derived from benchmark rows, not a published range — uppercase has never disclosed pay, and there is no careers page or ATS to scrape. All seven roles are PREDICTED, not listed: as of the profile research, the company site has no /careers page (12-page sitemap, all careers URLs 404), no Keka/Darwinbox/Zoho/Freshteam portal is theirs, and a filtered LinkedIn search on company id 79531488 returns zero live postings — the only role surfaced, "Institutional Sales Manager- West" (Mumbai), is ~4 months old and its URL now 301-redirects as expired, and in any case it is a manager seat, not a fresher one. Naukri, Instahyre and Jooble blocked automated access, so an unlisted opening on a board that could not be reached cannot be excluded. Two further cautions: the export's "Series B" label overstates the round (it is a flat Rs 20 Cr internal top-up, Rs 10 Cr each from Accel India and Volrado, at an unchanged ~Rs 534 Cr valuation), and the export's "parent: Acefour Accessories" is not a parent — Acefour Accessories Pvt. Ltd. is uppercase's own legal entity, so do not price this as a subsidiary of a larger group. Because the stage label is ambiguous and the company is small (~90-120 people), confidence is dropped one step from the "medium" carried by the underlying benchmark rows to low. Actual offers at a company this size vary more than any band, and the specific hiring manager matters more than the market rate.

salary_benchmarks.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

bands.note: Thinnest data of any row - no source I could reach breaks out pre-Series A separately. Built bottom-up: Payscale India Product Analyst averages Rs 5.12L for <1 yr and Rs 7.84L for 1-4 yrs (76 profiles, Jul 2026); Talent.com puts entry Product Analyst at Rs 8.0L. Then applied the only published early-stage adjustment I found - productmanagementjob.com's 'pre-seed to Series A: below market, often 10-25% under the national median, highest equity percentage' - to the Rs 12L median entry APM base. In practice product-analyst titles cluster Rs 6-9L here and APM titles Rs 10-14L. Variable is usually token (0-10%) at this stage; the gap between Rs 14L fixed and Rs 20L total is almost entirely ESOP notional, which is a large percentage of a tiny cap table - treat it as paper, not pay. Confidence low: extrapolated from stage-discount language, not from observed seed-stage offers.

Genuinely no direct data for this combination - I could not find a single source reporting seed-stage entry-level product pay outside the metros. Derived by applying the published non-metro adjustment (Davzon India Salary Guide 2026: 0.82x tier-2 multiplier, 0.75x for remote/tier-3; Beacon Filing: 'tier 2 cities typically run 15-30% below tier 1 equivalents') to the metro seed row, with the floor cross-checked against Payscale's 10th percentile of Rs 3.44L for Product Analyst India-wide and Davzon's junior business analyst band of Rs 4-7L. Confidence low and should be treated as a rough prior only - at this stage and location, individual offers vary far more than any band, and equity terms matter more than the cash number.

Best-supported startup row. Four independent write-ups converge: Product Leadership puts growth-stage startup APMs at Rs 12-22L, 'ESOP heavy', and its calculator returns Rs 12-16L base + Rs 2-4L variable + Rs 2-6L ESOP for a Series B+ mid-size entry PM; productmanagementjob.com gives entry APM base Rs 9-16.2L, median Rs 12L, total comp Rs 13.4L, with Series B-D 'at or slightly above median' plus 'meaningful options'; Recrew gives entry APM Rs 8-15L with a 0-2 yr average of Rs 15L. The Rs 8L low end is the product-analyst title (and analytics-flavoured APM roles), not a branded APM program. Bonus convention is 10-20% of base. Confidence medium rather than high because every source states company stage qualitatively and the LPA figures are not themselves cut by funding stage.

Series A-B companies outside Bengaluru/Gurugram/Mumbai are concentrated in Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai, Jaipur and Indore. Band derived by applying the tier-2 adjustment (Davzon 0.82x; Beacon Filing 15-30% below tier-1) to the metro Series A-B row. Directionally consistent with Indeed India's non-metro APM city averages (Hyderabad Rs 13.04L, Chennai Rs 13.02L, Noida Rs 12.51L) and with OnJob's statement that Hyderabad and Pune typically run 5-15% below Bengaluru - but those Indeed figures are all-experience averages, not filtered to 0-2 years, so they over-read the entry band. Confidence low: the adjustment is real and published, the underlying stage-specific non-metro data is not.

This is where the crowdsourced data actually concentrates, because late-stage startups and unicorns are what people report. Indeed India: APM average base Rs 16.39L (25 salaries, Aug 2026), low Rs 11.71L to high Rs 22.95L, Gurgaon Rs 20.14L and Bengaluru Rs 17.04L; named late-stage employers on that page include ShareChat Rs 22.14L and Slice Rs 22.00L. OnJob puts APM (0-2 yrs) total cash at Rs 12-28L, median Rs 18L, at 'product and funded-startup companies'. 6figr's India APM page reports an average of Rs 17L (I could only read that figure from the listing, the page body did not render for me). Product-analyst titles at the same companies sit lower - Indeed's India Product Analyst average base is Rs 12.70L (23 salaries) - which is why the fixed low is Rs 12L rather than higher. Total high adds ~10-15% variable plus roughly Rs 4-8L/yr of ESOP notional. Confidence medium, not high: sample sizes on Indeed are 23-25, and the title is applied inconsistently across levels.

Anchored on actual reported non-metro city numbers rather than a multiplier: Indeed India APM averages Hyderabad Rs 13.04L, Chennai Rs 13.02L, Noida Rs 12.51L; Indeed Product Analyst averages Chennai Rs 10.13L and Hyderabad Rs 7.42L. Cross-checked against OnJob (Hyderabad/Pune typically 5-15% below Bengaluru) and Product Leadership's all-level PM city index (Delhi NCR -12%, Hyderabad -17%, Pune -28%, Chennai -33% versus Bengaluru). Caveat that keeps this at medium rather than high: those city figures are all-experience averages for a junior-skewed title, not a clean 0-2 year cut, so the true entry band is probably at the lower half of what the averages imply. ESOP at Series C+ is real but usually a smaller multiple than at Series A-B, hence the narrower fixed-to-total gap.

Deliberately the widest band because this bucket is bimodal and averaging it would mislead. Lower mode - IT services, BFSI, listed non-tech: Jobaaj cites Rs 8-12L starting packages for entry-level product roles at IT services firms; Product Leadership puts service/traditional IT APMs at Rs 8-15L; Davzon puts a junior (0-2 yr) business analyst at Rs 4-7L and a junior PM at Rs 8-14L. Upper mode - branded APM programs and big-tech/listed consumer tech: Jobaaj reports top APM programs at Google, Microsoft, Meta, Flipkart, Zepto and PhonePe paying Rs 16-45L; Product Leadership puts tier-1 product companies at Rs 18-35L with ESOPs. The Rs 45L total high assumes an RSU-heavy big-tech APM offer where stock is 30-60% of total comp (productmanagementjob.com). Note Levels.fyi India shows a PM 25th percentile of Rs 29.2L and median Rs 44.6L total, but that is all levels and is badly skewed to senior big-tech PMs - do not read it as an entry-level number. Confidence medium.

Same bimodality as the metro row, compressed at the bottom but not at the top. Lower mode: IT services and shared-services entry analyst roles in Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Coimbatore and Indore run Rs 5-10L, consistent with Davzon's junior BA band of Rs 4-7L before its 0.82x tier-2 multiplier and Beacon Filing's 15-30% tier-2 discount (it cites a 36% Bangalore-to-Coimbatore gap for developers). Upper mode: global capability centres in Hyderabad and Pune pay at or near metro parity, which is why the high end stays at Rs 18L fixed / Rs 28L total rather than being multiplied down - Levels.fyi India business analyst city averages are Hyderabad Rs 19.58L and Pune Rs 18.66L, both above Mumbai's Rs 15.43L (all levels). Indeed's Product Analyst page lists large-employer outliers such as Amadeus Rs 19.33L and Sopra Steria Rs 19.00L. Confidence medium; read this row as two distributions, not one, and place a specific offer by employer type before city.

salary_benchmarks.family: Growth and performance marketing (entry-level, 0-2 years, India)

bands.note: Titles seed startups actually post: Growth Associate, Performance Marketing Associate/Executive, Paid Media Executive. AmbitionBox (Aug-Sep 2026 refresh): Growth Marketing Executive 0-1yr Rs4.3-4.8L, 1-3yr Rs5.1-5.6L (158 salaries); Performance Marketing Associate 0-1yr Rs2.8-4.1L, 1-3yr Rs4.7-5.7L (77); Growth Executive typical Rs4.3-4.8L (643); Growth Marketing Associate 1-3yr Rs4.0-4.4L (13, AmbitionBox itself flags medium confidence); Paid Media Executive 1-3yr Rs3.8-4.3L (353). Rs8L fixed is the realistic ceiling and needs a strong signal (tier-1 campus, prior D2C/agency internship with real ad-spend ownership, or a well-capitalised YC/Accel seed). ESOP is normal at this stage but for a 0-2yr hire the grant is small in notional terms (often 0.01-0.05%, roughly Rs0.5-1.5L/yr of paper) and should be discounted heavily - the Rs10L total-high assumes ~Rs1-1.5L notional ESOP plus a 5-10% variable. Confidence capped at medium because no source I could reach tags data by funding stage; the stage split is my inference from the title mix, not a sourced cut.

Extrapolated, not directly sourced - there is no reachable dataset that isolates seed-stage growth hires outside the metros, so treat this row as an estimate. Anchors used: AmbitionBox city cut for Digital Marketing Executive (Pune Rs3.2-3.5L, Hyderabad Rs3.3-3.7L vs Bengaluru/Mumbai Rs3.6-4.0L) and Indeed India (Digital Marketing Executive national average base Rs2.28L, 588 salaries, updated 25 May 2026; Pune Rs3.79L, Hyderabad Rs3.61L). The observed tier-2 discount at the executive band is only ~10-15%, but the seed ecosystem outside metros is thin and offers cluster low. Below roughly Rs3L this stops being a growth-marketing offer and becomes a general digital-marketing executive job. ESOP is often offered here but is close to worthless in cash terms at this stage - do not let it justify a fixed-cash number below Rs3.5L.

AmbitionBox Aug-Sep 2026: Performance Marketing Analyst 1-3yr Rs5.5-6.1L (32 salaries); Performance Marketing Associate 1-3yr Rs4.7-5.7L with reported points such as AdYogi Rs6.5L at 1yr; Marketing Associate Bengaluru Rs5.7-6.3L, Gurugram Rs5.6-6.2L, Mumbai Rs5.5-6.0L (4.4k salaries); Growth Executive Gurugram Rs5.2-6.5L; Senior Performance Marketing Executive 1-3yr Rs6.0-7.0L (371). Levels.fyi India Marketing 25th percentile total comp is Rs9.38L (verified offers, updated 10 Sep 2026) - a fair proxy for the junior end of the funded-startup sample. Rs12L fixed is the top of the band and generally requires an MBA or a demonstrated P&L/ad-spend track record. ESOP is standard and meaningful at A-B: assume Rs1.5-3L/yr notional over a 4-year vest plus a 10% variable to reach the Rs16L total-high. Medium confidence: the underlying salary counts are good, but the stage attribution is inferred.

Thin evidence - marked low deliberately. AmbitionBox city cuts show only a small tier-2 discount at associate level (Marketing Associate Pune Rs5.3-6.0L vs Bengaluru Rs5.7-6.3L; Digital Marketing Associate Pune Rs3.8-4.2L, Hyderabad Rs4.0-4.4L vs Bengaluru Rs4.0-4.5L), but Levels.fyi's aggregate city medians show a much wider gap at the funded-company end (Hyderabad Rs9.03L vs Bengaluru Rs19.83L, updated 10 Sep 2026), which is what drags this band down versus the metro row. Practically, most Series A-B companies hiring outside the metros are in Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad or Jaipur, and the sample is too small for anyone to publish a clean band. ESOP is offered on the same terms as the metro row; the discount is almost entirely in fixed cash.

This band is genuinely wide because two different hires sit in it. A non-MBA growth/performance analyst promoted in lands Rs8-13L fixed; a tier-1 MBA or premium campus growth hire lands Rs14-18L, occasionally Rs20L+. Evidence (AmbitionBox, Aug-Sep 2026): Growth Manager India 1-3yr Rs12.9-14.3L (553 salaries in that bucket, 3.2k overall); Growth Marketing Manager 1-3yr Rs11.8-15.2L (915); Performance Marketing Manager 1-3yr Rs8.5-10.4L (2.8k). Company pages: PhonePe growth manager Rs11.5-17.1L for 2-7yrs (30 salaries, AmbitionBox high confidence), Unacademy Rs11.6-15.6L for 1-8yrs (34, high confidence), Zepto 1-3yr estimated Rs12.8-18.9L, Razorpay 1-3yr estimated Rs13.6-19.4L, Groww 3-6yr Rs19.7-29.5L. City premium is real: Growth Manager Bengaluru Rs17.1-18.9L, Gurugram Rs16.6-18.5L, Mumbai Rs15.6-18.0L. Total-high of Rs26L assumes 15-20% variable plus Rs3-6L/yr notional ESOP - and at C+ that ESOP is worth more than at earlier stages because secondaries and buybacks are common. Note the 'Manager' title inflation: many of these 1-3yr datapoints are post-MBA, so a 0-2yr non-MBA candidate should anchor to the lower half.

Low confidence: very few Series C+ companies run growth teams outside Bengaluru/Gurugram/Mumbai, so no source publishes this cut and I am extrapolating. Anchors: AmbitionBox Growth Manager Noida Rs14.2-17.4L and New Delhi Rs15.1-17.0L versus Bengaluru Rs17.1-18.9L (a ~10-20% step down for near-metro NCR, and the step is steeper for true tier-2); Performance Marketing Manager New Delhi Rs12.9-14.2L versus Bengaluru Rs16.1-17.8L; PhysicsWallah (Noida) growth manager Rs9.7-14.0L at 3-4yrs (3 salaries, AmbitionBox low confidence). Levels.fyi's Hyderabad marketing median of Rs9.03L versus Bengaluru Rs19.83L supports a material discount. In practice the credible employers here are Chennai SaaS (Freshworks, Zoho, Chargebee), Hyderabad (Darwinbox), Pune and Ahmedabad D2C. ESOP terms usually match the metro row; the cut is in fixed cash.

This row is strongly bimodal and the single number is misleading unless you split it. LOW MODE - media/creative agencies and IT services (GroupM/WPP Media, Publicis, Omnicom, Accenture, Infosys): AmbitionBox shows WPP Media performance marketing manager Rs7.1-10.5L across 23 salaries, Publicis Media/Publicis Global Delivery performance marketing analyst Rs6.0L at 3yrs, Accenture digital marketing associate Rs4.8L at 2yrs. Entry-level here is Rs5.5-8L fixed with little or no equity and a 5-10% variable. HIGH MODE - listed/late-stage consumer internet and global tech (Swiggy, Eternal/Zomato, Meesho, Amazon, Nykaa): Swiggy growth manager 1-3yr Rs17.4-25.9L (overall Rs20.5-23.6L across 48 salaries, AmbitionBox high confidence), Meesho growth manager 3-6yr Rs37.7-44.4L, Amazon performance marketing associate Rs12.6L at 3yrs, Lenskart performance marketing manager 3-6yr Rs16.6-18.4L. Levels.fyi India Marketing (verified offers, updated 10 Sep 2026): median total comp Rs16.44L, 25th percentile Rs9.38L, 75th Rs26.58L, with Bengaluru at Rs19.83L, Mumbai Rs13.79L, Gurgaon Rs11.56L. Total-high of Rs26L reflects the high mode with RSUs plus a 10-15% cash bonus. If the offer in front of you is from an agency, benchmark against the low mode only.

The best-sourced non-metro row, because large employers report at volume in tier-2. AmbitionBox (Sep 2026, 47.9k salaries): Digital Marketing Executive 0-1yr Rs2.5-2.8L and 1-3yr Rs2.9-3.2L nationally, with Pune Rs3.2-3.5L, Hyderabad Rs3.3-3.7L, Chennai-area comparable; Digital Marketing Specialist 1-3yr Rs3.9-4.4L nationally with Chennai Rs5.4-5.9L and Pune Rs6.3-6.9L on the blended average; Marketing Associate Pune Rs5.3-6.0L. Indeed India: Digital Marketing Executive average base Rs2.28L (588 salaries, 25 May 2026) with Bengaluru Rs3.85L, Pune Rs3.79L, Hyderabad Rs3.61L; the Marketing Executive page (2.4k salaries, 30 Jun 2026) gives a Rs1.28L-Rs4.19L spread. The Rs12L top of the band is captured by global-capability-centre roles such as Amazon Hyderabad or Chennai SaaS, not by domestic firms. Levels.fyi Hyderabad marketing median Rs9.03L (all levels) supports that upper tail. Equity is RSU-based at MNCs and near-zero at domestic large employers; variable is typically 5-10%.

salary_benchmarks.family: Management trainee and graduate leadership programmes (India, 0-2 years experience) — business-side/non-engineering entry-level: MT, GET-equivalent business tracks, graduate leadership/rotational programmes, founder's office & chief-of-staff associate, business/growth associate, entry-level business analyst

bands.note: Seed companies almost never run a named 'management trainee programme'; the equivalent is a founder's office / chief-of-staff / business-associate hire. Anchors: letsenterprise.in puts early-stage startup freshers at Rs 3-5 LPA and non-tech freshers at Rs 3-5 LPA standard with good companies at Rs 8-10 LPA; Beyond Campus (2026) puts founder's-office freshers at Rs 6-12 LPA for Series A-C, so seed sits at the bottom of that; Internshala's live founder's-office/CoS fresher listings for 2025-26 grads run Rs 9,975 to Rs 98,881 per month (Rs 1.2L to Rs 11.9L annualised), confirming a very long right tail from a handful of well-funded repeat-founder companies. Fixed high of 9 is the realistic ceiling for a non-IIM/non-IIT candidate; 10-12 LPA fixed exists but only at Peak XV/Accel-seeded companies hiring off tier-1 campuses. Variable is usually nil or token at this stage. Total-comp high of 14 is fixed 9 plus roughly Rs 4-5L/yr of paper ESOP (seed pools are 8-12 percent fully diluted; a junior grant is 0.05-0.15 percent vesting over 4 years) — treat that ESOP as lottery-ticket value, not cash, and do not accept a fixed-cash discount for it. Confidence medium: the stage-specific India numbers come from two or three sources rather than a large panel.

Genuinely thin data — no source I found reports seed-stage, non-metro, business-side entry pay directly. This row is an extrapolation, flagged as such. Construction: the metro seed band (4.5-9 fixed) discounted by the 15-30 percent tier-1-to-tier-2 gap that multiple India city-comparison sources report, floored by the broad-market Indian management-trainee baseline — Indeed India shows an all-India MT average of Rs 37,087/month (Rs 4.45 LPA) with a floor of Rs 18,147/month (Rs 2.18 LPA) across 125 salaries updated 29 July 2026, and PayScale India shows entry-level (under 1 year) Manager Trainee average total comp of Rs 4,41,784 with a 10th-percentile base of Rs 1.93L (92 profiles, updated 23 June 2026). Cross-check: hyring.com puts tier-3 MBA freshers at Rs 3-6 LPA, which is the same population. ESOP at a seed company outside the metros is worth close to nothing on a risk-adjusted basis, so total high is only modestly above fixed high.

Best-evidenced startup row. Beyond Campus (2026) states Rs 6-12 LPA for founder's-office freshers at Series A-C companies, with top-tier startups higher; letsenterprise.in independently puts well-funded growth-stage startup freshers at Rs 5-9 LPA. Glassdoor India cross-checks the metro envelope: Management Trainee in Bangalore averages Rs 7,50,000/yr with a 25th-75th of Rs 5,00,000 to Rs 12,23,750; Gurgaon averages Rs 6,80,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 4,50,000 to Rs 11,90,000. So 6-12 fixed is well supported for Bengaluru and Gurugram; Mumbai runs higher (see the listed/large row). Variable at this stage is typically 5-10 percent of fixed and often paid on company rather than individual targets. Total high of 16 assumes 12 fixed plus about 1 LPA variable plus roughly Rs 3 LPA/yr of ESOP paper value (Series A pools are 12-15 percent; junior grants cluster at 0.05-0.1 percent, per incorpx). Judgement rule: at Series A-B an offer under 6 LPA fixed in these three cities is below market for a graduate business hire regardless of how the ESOP is described.

Extrapolated, not directly measured — I found no source reporting Series A-B business-side entry pay for Pune, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Indore, Kochi, Chandigarh or Coimbatore specifically. Method: metro Series A-B band (6-12) taken to 70-85 percent, the tier-2-vs-tier-1 ratio that India city-comparison sources report, then sanity-checked against measured non-metro points from Indeed India's MT city table (Pune Rs 64,417/month = Rs 7.73 LPA, Hyderabad Rs 49,422/month = Rs 5.93 LPA, Noida Rs 48,163/month = Rs 5.78 LPA, 125 salaries, 29 July 2026) and against hyring.com's tier-2 MBA fresher band of Rs 6-10 LPA. Caveat: Pune and Hyderabad behave more like metros for funded startups than like true tier-2 cities, so an offer in either can legitimately sit at or slightly above this band's high. Total high assumes fixed 8, modest variable, and thin ESOP.

Late-stage and unicorn business-side graduate hiring. letsenterprise.in puts unicorn/late-stage freshers at Rs 8-12 LPA, which sets the floor and the middle. The upper half comes from Levels.fyi India (filtered to entry-level Business Analyst, last updated 10 September 2026): all-India median total comp Rs 10,84,011 with 25th Rs 7,66,411, 75th Rs 14,91,217, 90th Rs 18,10,000; Greater Bengaluru median Rs 12,26,071 with 25th Rs 7,92,340, 75th Rs 16,48,623, 90th Rs 18,50,000. Important caveat on that source: Levels.fyi's India business-analyst sample skews toward GCCs, big tech and banks (its top-paying employers on that page are Google, Amazon, Flipkart, Citi, Accenture), so it flatters a pure Series C startup MT offer — I used it for the ceiling, not the centre. Variable at Series C+ is typically 10-15 percent and ESOPs are real (buyback programmes exist), worth roughly Rs 2-4 LPA/yr on a junior grant. Total high of 22 is fixed 16 plus variable plus ESOP plus a joining bonus. Confidence medium rather than high because no source measures 'Series C+ non-engineering management trainee' as its own cut.

Sparse. Late-stage startups concentrate business hiring in Bengaluru, Gurugram and Mumbai, so the non-metro population here is mostly city-ops, supply and category roles in Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Chennai, Jaipur, Lucknow and similar — and those pay materially below HQ-based analyst roles. Construction: unicorn/late-stage fresher band of Rs 8-12 LPA (letsenterprise.in) discounted 15-25 percent for location, floored by Levels.fyi's all-India entry-level BA 25th percentile of Rs 7,66,411 and Indeed's non-metro MT points (Hyderabad Rs 5.93 LPA, Noida Rs 5.78 LPA, all-India average Rs 4.45 LPA). Marked low confidence because it is a derived figure, not an observed distribution. If the role is a city-ops or field role rather than an HQ analyst role, expect the bottom of this band plus a large sales/ops incentive component.

This band is deliberately wide because the market is genuinely bimodal, and that split is the single most important thing when judging an offer. Cluster A, the elite graduate leadership programmes recruiting from IIM-ABC/XLRI/ISB: HUL ULIP Rs 22-28 LPA, ITC IBD Rs 20-25 LPA, Nestle/P&G Rs 18-30 LPA, Aditya Birla Group MBA track Rs 8-15 LPA (salaryinsight.in, 2026); Prosple lists Aditya Birla MT at Rs 8-8.5 LPA average. Cluster B, mainstream corporate MT — banking MTs at SBI/HDFC/ICICI Rs 6-12 LPA, manufacturing MTs at Tata Steel/JSW/L&T Rs 8-15 LPA, non-MBA conglomerate MTs Rs 5-10 LPA. Glassdoor India measures the blended distribution: all-India MT average total pay Rs 7,25,000 with 25th Rs 4,67,500 and 75th Rs 11,00,000; Mumbai average Rs 10,00,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 6,00,000 to Rs 15,12,500; Bangalore average Rs 7,50,000 with 25th-75th of Rs 5,00,000 to Rs 12,23,750. 6figr shows Mumbai MT averaging about Rs 13 LPA, but that sample skews to people well past the 0-2 year mark, so treat it as an upper reference only. Fixed high of 18 reflects that a Rs 22-28 LPA elite-programme CTC is typically Rs 16-20 LPA fixed once variable, retention and one-time components are stripped out; total high of 30 is the top of the P&G/Nestle range. Michael Page's India Salary Guide 2026 puts increments at 8-12 percent, so year-two progression from any of these anchors is modest. High confidence: four or more independent sources agree on the shape and the levels.

The largest population in this whole family by headcount — BPO/ITES and shared-services MT programmes, bank probationary/MT cadres, and manufacturing MT postings at plant towns. Low end: Genpact Management Trainee, whose India footprint is heavily Hyderabad, Kolkata and Jaipur, reports Rs 3.6-6.7 LPA on AmbitionBox and Rs 5,35,000-11,12,500 (25th-75th) on Glassdoor across 1,616 submissions, with Indeed at about Rs 6.46 LPA. Broad market: Indeed India MT average Rs 37,087/month (Rs 4.45 LPA), range Rs 18,147-75,792/month (Rs 2.18-9.09 LPA), 125 salaries updated 29 July 2026; PayScale India Manager Trainee entry-level (under 1 year) average total comp Rs 4,41,784 and early-career (1-4 years) Rs 4,76,017, 92 profiles updated 23 June 2026. High end: manufacturing MT programmes at Tata Steel, JSW and L&T sit at Rs 8-15 LPA (salaryinsight.in) and are located at Jamshedpur, Vijayanagar and similar non-metro sites, which is why fixed high is 12 rather than 8. Reality check on expectations from Naukri JobSpeak 2026: 73 percent of Indian undergraduates expect above Rs 5 LPA but only 40 percent actually receive an offer at that level — so a Rs 4.5-5 LPA MT offer outside the metros is at or slightly above median, not a lowball. ESOP is not part of the package in this row; total high of 16 is fixed plus performance bonus and shift/location allowances.

salary_benchmarks.family: Product analyst and associate product manager (APM) — entry level, 0–2 years, India

bands.note: Widest band in the table because seed pay is founder-dependent, not market-set. Live Wellfound postings in Bengaluru/Gurugram show the real spread: APM Bengaluru Rs 4.5-6L and Rs 5-8L (remote India) at the bottom, PM roles at Rs 3-6L in HSR Layout, up to 'Associate Product Manager (Technical)' Bengaluru at Rs 12-18L and a Gurgaon technical PM at Rs 14-24L with 0.1-1.0% equity. Fixed low of 6 is a product-analyst/APM-generalist offer at an unbranded seed company; 14 is a well-funded seed (Accel/Blume/Peak XV pre-A) hiring an IIT/IIM or ex-APM-program candidate. Variable pay is usually zero at this stage. Total high of 18 = Rs 14L fixed plus notional ESOP only: typical grant 0.05-0.30% on a Rs 40-100 Cr post-money, i.e. roughly Rs 2-8L of paper value spread over a 4-year vest with a 1-year cliff, so about Rs 1-4L/yr notional and realistically worth zero. Do not treat the ESOP as cash when judging an offer here. Confidence medium not high: postings are real and current but few seed companies report CTC to AmbitionBox/Glassdoor, so there is no large-sample check on this band. Within the band, product analyst titles sit in the bottom third (6-9) and APM titles in the top half (10-14).

This is the weakest cell in the table and I am openly extrapolating. There is no stage-tagged salary dataset for seed startups in Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Indore, Jaipur, Kochi or Kolkata — the sample sizes collapse (AmbitionBox has 63 product-analyst salaries for all of Pune, 92 APM salaries for all of Ahmedabad). What I anchored on: AmbitionBox product analyst Pune typical band Rs 8.9-11L with a 1-3 yr average of only Rs 6.7L, AmbitionBox APM Ahmedabad 1-3 yrs average Rs 11.2L (but that pool is dominated by mid-size product/services firms, not seed startups), Cutshort's model showing PM pay in Ahmedabad Rs 13.6L, Coimbatore Rs 12.8L and Bhubaneswar Rs 12L versus Rs 20L in Bengaluru, and Wellfound's remote-India APM postings at Rs 5-8L. I applied roughly a 30-35% discount to the metro seed band. Treat 4.5-9 as an educated bracket, not a benchmark. Variable is essentially nil; ESOP at a non-metro seed company is worth even less in practice, so total high of 11 is 9 fixed plus about 2 of notional paper.

Anchors that converge here: AmbitionBox APM India 1-3 yrs average Rs 13.1L (15.5k salaries, updated 6 Sep 2026); Cutshort's startup-focused calculator for a 2-year PM gives minimum Rs 9.9L, average Rs 15.2L, top paymasters Rs 24.3L; Levels.fyi entry-level PM India 25th percentile Rs 9.97L and median Rs 15.69L (updated 10 Sep 2026); Glassdoor Bengaluru APM 25th percentile Rs 11.94L.
